achievements.en: Three first-author papers: enough to defend.
A paper at a top venue.

achievements.zh: 读论文时冒出五个想法。
被拒六次，反手中了三篇。
那封阴阳怪气的回复居然奏效了。

achievements.en: It never even reached the reviewers.
achievements.zh: 连审稿人的面都没见到。

achievements.en: A reviewer raised the flaw you'd already fixed.
achievements.zh: 审稿人指出的问题，你早就修好了。

achievements.en: Overtime eight weeks in a row.
Survived an outage on deadline day.
achievements.zh: 截稿当天 Overleaf 宕机，你挺过来了。
熬过了一次地狱级排队。

achievements.en: Survived a very long IRB review.
achievements.zh: 熬过了一次超长的伦理审查 (IRB)。

achievements.en: Burned out for the first time. It passes with rest.
achievements.zh: 第一次倦怠。休息一阵就会过去。
倦怠过两次，还是毕业了。
挺过了假期后的邮件轰炸。

achievements.en: Presented in the clothes you flew in.
achievements.zh: 穿着飞机上那身衣服做了报告。
偶像停在了你的海报前。

achievements.en: Visa trouble forced a remote talk.
achievements.zh: 签证出了问题，只能远程做报告。

achievements.en: Got the Kind and Funded advisor.
achievements.zh: 抽到了人好钱多的导师。

achievements.en: The Kind and Funded advisor took another student the year you started.
achievements.zh: 你入学那年，那位人好钱多的导师收了别人。

achievements.en: 20 in-person lab meetings with the Kind and Funded advisor.
achievements.zh: 和人好钱多的导师线下开了 20 次组会。

achievements.en: A paper your Kind and Funded advisor found no orphan words in.
achievements.zh: 人好钱多的导师翻遍你的论文，没找到一个独占一行的单词。
Judy Olson 的十个问题，你答得滴水不漏。

achievements.en: Wore the doctoral hood backwards at commencement.
achievements.zh: 毕业典礼上把博士垂布戴反了。

achievements.en: Graduated in four years or less.
Graduated in year seven or later.

achievements.zh: 拿到了实习的转正 offer。
多局下来，看遍了全部 26 个结局。

advisors.en: Famous but Absent
advisors.zh: 放养型大牛

advisors.en: A big name in the field, usually somewhere else.
advisors.zh: 名气很大，行踪全靠朋友圈定位。

advisors.en: Micromanager
advisors.zh: 圈养型

advisors.en: Checks every detail, down to your commit messages.
advisors.zh: 连你的 commit message 都要逐条过目。

advisors.en: Hungry Assistant Prof
advisors.zh: 卷王青椒

advisors.en: New to the job and hungry for papers.
advisors.zh: 非升即走倒计时中，求文若渴。

advisors.en: Kind but Unfunded
advisors.zh: 两袖清风型

advisors.en: Fights for their students on almost no budget.
advisors.zh: 经费几乎为零，护犊子满分。

advisors.en: Grant Machine
advisors.zh: 基金收割机

advisors.en: Never short of funding, or of grant reports to write.
advisors.zh: 不差钱，也不差待写的结题报告。

advisors.en: The Visionary
advisors.zh: 画饼型

advisors.en: Big ideas, and a new one every week.
advisors.zh: 饼很大，而且每周都换新口味。

advisors.en: Industry Joint
advisors.zh: 校企两栖型

advisors.en: Half professor, half tech company.
advisors.zh: 工牌两张，人只有一个。

advisors.en: Near Retirement
advisors.zh: 佛系老教授

advisors.en: A legend of the field, counting down to retirement.
advisors.zh: 江湖传说，退休倒计时中。

advisors.en: Serial Founder
advisors.zh: 斜杠创业型

advisors.en: Three startups, and nobody is sure which one is real.
advisors.zh: 名下三家创业公司，哪家是真的，至今成谜。

advisors.en: Methods Purist
advisors.zh: 方法洁癖型

advisors.en: No result survives without ten seeds and a significance test.
advisors.zh: 少于十个种子、没做显著性检验的结果，一律按玄学处理。

advisors.en: Kind and Funded
advisors.zh: 人好钱多型

advisors.en: Kind and well funded, with no patience for borderline work.
advisors.zh: 人好，经费足，就是见不得“差不多就行”。

advisors.en: Meticulous about layout and visual detail: orphan words, consistent capitalization, figure fonts.
advisors.zh: 对排版和视觉细节一丝不苟：独占一行的单词、大小写是否统一、图里的字体。

advisors.en: Always finds the major flaw, and asks the hard but critical question.
advisors.zh: 总能找出重大缺陷，问出那个难回答但关键的问题。

advisors.en: Replies at strange hours, midnight included, always adding "no need to reply until Monday".
advisors.zh: 常在奇怪的时间回复，半夜也不例外，而且总会加一句“周一之前不用回”。

advisors.en: Buys bubble tea for everyone who comes to lab meeting in person.
advisors.zh: 会给每个线下来开组会的人买奶茶。

advisors.en: Replies to email at 3 am.
advisors.zh: 凌晨 3 点回邮件。

advisors.en: Loves Gantt charts.
advisors.zh: 对甘特图爱得深沉。

advisors.en: Always wants "just one more experiment".
advisors.zh: 口头禅是“再补一个实验就好”。

advisors.en: Draws everything on a whiteboard.
advisors.zh: 什么都要在白板上画出来。

advisors.en: Forgets meetings, then remembers them better than you do.
advisors.zh: 经常忘记开会，事后却记得比你还清楚。

advisors.en: Sends papers with no message, only the PDF.
advisors.zh: 转论文从不附言，只甩一个 PDF。

advisors.en: Writes "great!!" on everything and means it 40% of the time.
advisors.zh: 什么都批“很好！！”，其中 40% 是真心的。

advisors.en: Insists on tables over figures.
advisors.zh: 能用表格，绝不画图。

advisors.en: Only meets while walking.
advisors.zh: 只在散步时开会。

advisors.en: Seems to know every reviewer personally.
advisors.zh: 审稿人好像个个都是老熟人。

advisors.en: Has a favorite font and enforces it.
advisors.zh: 有一款本命字体，全组都得用。

advisors.en: Plays devil's advocate even when agreeing with you.
advisors.zh: 就算同意你，也要先杠一下。

advisors.en: Answers questions with questions.
advisors.zh: 总拿问题回答问题。

advisors.en: Remembers every student's birthday.
advisors.zh: 记得每个学生的生日。

advisors.en: Brings snacks to lab meeting.
advisors.zh: 开组会总带零食。

advisors.en: Says "let's write a grant about it" about everything.
advisors.zh: 万物皆可“申个基金”。

advisors.en: Keeps a list of every idea anyone has ever had in lab meeting.
advisors.zh: 记着组会上每个人提过的每一个想法。

advisors.en: Takes calls from the car, always slightly out of signal.
advisors.zh: 总在车里接电话，信号永远差一点。

advisors.en: Prefers a 2-hour meeting to a 2-line email.
advisors.zh: 宁可开 2 小时的会，也不发 2 行的邮件。

advisors.en: Has strong opinions about the Oxford comma.
advisors.zh: 对牛津逗号有执念。

advisors.en: Quotes papers from the 1990s from memory.
advisors.zh: 90 年代的论文张口就来。

advisors.en: Reads drafts on paper, with a red pen.
advisors.zh: 稿子要打印出来，拿红笔批。

advisors.en: Schedules meetings in 25-minute blocks.
advisors.zh: 按 25 分钟一格排会。

advisors.en: Responds to long emails with a single emoji.
advisors.zh: 长邮件一律用一个表情打发。

advisors.en: Keeps a plant in the lab that nobody else may water.
advisors.zh: 在实验室养了一盆植物，别人不许浇水。

advisors.en: Always asks "what's the one-sentence version?"
advisors.zh: 总问：“能一句话说清楚吗？”

advisors.en: Starts every meeting with "so, what did we learn this week?"
advisors.zh: 每次开会的开场白都是：“所以，这周我们学到了什么？”

advisors.en: Has a standing Friday-afternoon reading group nobody can escape.
advisors.zh: 有个雷打不动的周五下午读书会，谁也逃不掉。

code.en: Your advisor seems a little cooler toward you.
code.zh: 导师对你好像冷淡了一点。

code.en: The lab feels a little colder.
Your friends are glad to see you.
Your friends haven't heard from you in a while.
code.zh: 朋友们好久没在群里见到你了。

code.en: More people in the field know your name.
code.zh: 圈子里知道你名字的人多了。

code.en: You feel a bit out of the loop.
code.zh: 你感觉有点跟圈子脱节了。

code.en: Your sense for good problems sharpens.
code.zh: 你挑好问题的眼光更准了。
你开始怀疑自己的研究直觉。

code.en: Your code feels less fragile than last month.
code.zh: 代码没上个月那么容易崩了。

code.en: Your writing feels a little sharper.
You feel steadier in front of a room.
code.zh: 当众讲话时，你更有底气了。

code.en: Presenting feels harder than it used to.
code.zh: 做报告好像比以前难了。

code.en: You understand the field a little better.
code.zh: 你对这个领域又懂了一点。

code.en: You feel behind on the literature.
code.zh: 你感觉自己落下了好多新论文。

code.en: {project} goes back to the idea stage.
That may help with the reviewers.
code.zh: 这在审稿人那里可能加分。

code.en: The reviewers may not like that.
“{paper}” keeps getting cited: {n} times and counting.
code.zh: “{paper}”的引用还在涨，已经 {n} 次了。

code.en: You bring a half-finished project from your Master's: “{title}”.
code.zh: 你把硕士时做了一半的项目也带来了：“{title}”。
{deadline} 剩 2 周 · 周末无休

code.en: You're on leave, so resting is the job.
code.zh: 你在休学，休息就是正事。

code.en: You come back from burnout knowing your limits a little better. New trait: Burnout Survivor.
code.zh: 你从倦怠里缓过来了，也更摸得清自己的极限。新特质：倦怠过来人。

code.en: “{title}” is due in two weeks and it's still in {stage}.
code.zh: “{title}”两周后截稿，可现在还在{stage}阶段。

code.en: You catch something nasty. The next two weeks will be slow.
code.zh: 你得了场重感冒，接下来两周干啥都慢半拍。

code.en: You burn out. For the next several weeks you'll get half as much done and can't crunch, so rest. It happens to more people than will ever say so.
code.zh: 你倦怠了。接下来几周效率减半，也没法冲刺，先好好休息。这事比你想的常见，只是很少有人说出口。

code.en: Your health is slipping: you'll get sick more often and work a little slower. Recharging helps, and so does saying yes to the gym or a hike when it comes up.
code.zh: 你的健康在走下坡路：更容易生病，干活也会慢一点。多休息充电，有人约你健身或爬山时也别总推掉。

code.en: You're running on fumes: with Energy this low, everything gets less done. Two weeks of recharging help.
code.zh: 你快没电了：精力这么低，做什么都要打折扣。休息充电两周会好些。

code.en: Your stress is high. Recharging and the good things that come up (friends, trips, hobbies) bring it down; at 100 you burn out.
code.zh: 你压力很大。休息充电和生活里的好事（朋友、旅行、爱好）都能帮你减压；压力到 100 就会倦怠。

code.en: While reading, you have an idea worth keeping.
code.zh: 读着读着，你冒出一个值得记下来的想法。

code.en: {name} adds you as a co-author on their submission. You helped more than you realized.
code.zh: {name} 投稿时把你加进了作者列表。原来你帮的忙比自己以为的还多。

code.en: You're a TA for {course} this semester. Two days a turn go to teaching.
code.zh: 这学期你给“{course}”当助教，每轮有两天要花在教学上。

code.en: Why does anyone need this? Right now the case for novelty is the weakest part of the paper.
code.zh: 谁会需要这个？现在整篇论文最站不住的，就是创新点。

code.en: Does the evidence actually support the claim? Right now it doesn't quite.
code.zh: 证据真撑得住这个结论吗？现在看还差点意思。

code.en: A reader will get lost by section 3. What is the one sentence they must remember?
code.zh: 读者读到第 3 节就晕了。你想让他们记住的那一句话，到底是什么？

code.en: {name} is graduating and leaves a half-finished project.
code.zh: {name} 要毕业了，留下一个烂尾项目。

code.en: A senior student is graduating and leaves a half-finished project.
code.zh: 一位高年级同学要毕业了，留下一个烂尾项目。

code.en: Take it over, or start your own?
“{title}” is a rough draft. It can go in as it is; a more finished draft reads better.
code.zh: “{title}”还只是个粗糙的初稿。就这么投也行，只是稿子越完整，审稿人读着越顺。

code.en: “{title}” is barely drafted. Unless the next two weeks go very well, it won't be ready in time.
code.zh: “{title}”才刚起了个头。除非接下来两周特别顺利，否则赶不上。

code.en: Two weeks before the deadline, {advisor} reads “{title}” and asks one question: “{question}”
code.zh: 截稿前两周，{advisor}看完“{title}”，只问了一个问题：“{question}”

code.en: {name}'s paper, with you as a co-author, is in Findings at {venue}.
code.zh: 你和 {name} 合作的论文进了 {venue} 的 Findings。

code.en: {name}'s paper, with you as a co-author, is in at {venue}.
code.zh: 你和 {name} 合作的论文中了 {venue}。

code.en: {name}'s paper, with you as a co-author, didn't make it. {name} shrugs and starts revising.
code.zh: 你和 {name} 合作的论文没中。{name} 耸耸肩，开始改稿。

code.en: “{title}” didn't make the main conference, but Findings will take it.
code.zh: “{title}”没进主会，但 Findings 愿意收。

code.en: Address the reviews and try again.
code.zh: 按审稿意见修改，再试一次。
连审稿人的面都没见着。

code.en: Camera-ready: the {n} fixes you promised in the rebuttal will take {days} days next turn.
code.zh: 终稿：你在 rebuttal 里答应的 {n} 处修改，下一轮要花 {days} 天。

code.en: Something about “{title}” catches on. People keep citing it.
code.zh: “{title}”不知怎么就火了，引用蹭蹭往上涨。

code.en: After five rejections, the next one stings a little less. New trait: Rejection-Hardened.
code.zh: 被拒五次之后，再被拒也没那么疼了。新特质：久拒成钢。

code.en: Your visa didn't come through in time. You'll present “{title}” remotely, at 3 am your time.
code.zh: 签证没能及时下来，你只能线上讲“{title}”，时间是你这边的凌晨 3 点。

code.en: Apply for a student travel grant
Your advisor will pay for the trip.
Your lab has no travel money.
You fly to {city} for {venue} and present “{title}”. Four days of talks, posters and too much coffee.
code.zh: 你飞到{city}参加 {venue}，讲了“{title}”。四天特种兵式开会：报告、海报，外加喝不完的咖啡。

code.en: Your visa didn't come through, so you present “{title}” at {venue} remotely, at 3 am your time.
code.zh: 签证没下来，你只好线上参加 {venue}，在你这边的凌晨 3 点讲了“{title}”。

code.en: A student travel grant comes through.
code.zh: 学生差旅资助批下来了。

code.en: There's no travel money, so you present “{title}” at {venue} remotely. Two people ask great questions.
code.zh: 没有差旅经费，你只好线上参加 {venue}，讲了“{title}”。倒是有两个人问了很好的问题。

code.en: Best when they're testing what you know.
code.zh: 对方在考你懂不懂时最管用。

code.en: Best when they've found a real weakness.
code.zh: 对方真抓到弱点时最管用。

code.en: Best when they're asking why it matters.
code.zh: 对方问“这有什么意义”时最管用。
能拖点时间，但很少够用。
对方想要的是直截了当的回答。

code.en: They had found a real weakness; owning it would have landed better.
code.zh: 对方确实抓到了弱点；大方承认效果会更好。

code.en: They were asking why it matters; reframing would have helped.
code.zh: 对方问的是意义何在；换个角度回答会更好。

code.en: It was a trap; acknowledging or reframing beats a direct answer.
code.zh: 这题是个坑；承认局限或换个角度，都比直接回答强。

code.en: Five people, two hours, one room. Read each question and choose how to answer.
code.zh: 五个人，两小时，一间屋。看清每个问题，选好怎么答。

code.en: The committee takes turns. Read each question and choose how to answer.
code.zh: 委员们轮流发问。看清每个问题，选好怎么答。

code.en: They nod and write something down.
code.zh: 对方点点头，记了点什么。
对方满意地说了句“不错”。
对方被说服了，接着问下一题。

code.en: A long pause. They follow up.
code.zh: 沉默了好一会儿，对方又追问了一句。

code.en: You can see them making a note.
That one will come up again.
code.zh: 这个问题之后还会被翻出来。

code.en: You don't pass on the second try. The program offers you a Master's degree on the way out.
code.zh: 第二次还是没过。系里发了个硕士学位，送你体面离场。

code.en: Not this time. You can retake quals next year.
code.zh: 这次没过，明年还能再战。

code.en: Your proposal passes. You are officially a PhD candidate. The defense can come a year from now.
code.zh: 开题过了。你正式成为博士候选人，一年后就能答辩。

code.en: The committee asks you to revise the plan and present again in a few weeks.
code.zh: 委员会让你修改计划，几周后再讲一次。

code.en: They ask you to step outside. Ten long minutes later: “Congratulations, Doctor.”
code.zh: 他们请你先出去等等。度秒如年的十分钟后：“恭喜你，博士。”

code.en: You pass, with minor revisions. Two more weeks of fixes and you're done.
code.zh: 通过，但要小修。再改两周就搞定了。

code.en: You pass, with major revisions. Six weeks of work, then a short follow-up meeting.
code.zh: 通过，但要大修。还得改六周，最后再开个简短的跟进会。

code.en: Your job talk goes well. People keep asking follow-ups at dinner.
code.zh: 你的 job talk 很成功，饭桌上大家还在追着问。

code.en: The talk is fine. Not your best, not your worst.
code.zh: 报告中规中矩。没出高光，也没翻车。

code.en: It's September. You have five years, give or take, to become an expert in something nobody fully understands yet. Each turn is two weeks: choose what to focus on, keep an eye on Energy, Stress and Health, and remember: everyone else is also figuring it out.
code.zh: 现在是九月。你大概有五年时间，在一个还没人完全搞懂的方向上成为专家。每轮两周：选好专心做什么，留意精力、压力和健康。还有，别慌：大家都是第一次读博。

code.en: Your committee is formed and you have {n} first-author papers. The thesis proposal turns you from a student into a candidate. You'd present in {weeks} weeks.
code.zh: 委员会组好了，你也有了 {n} 篇一作论文。开题之后，你就从博士生变成了博士候选人。现在安排的话，{weeks} 周后上台报告。

code.en: You have {n} first-author papers accepted and one under review. You could start defense preparation now and hope the third one lands. Prep takes about three months.
code.zh: 你有 {n} 篇一作论文中稿，还有一篇在审。现在就可以开始准备答辩，一边祈祷第三篇也能中。准备大约要三个月。

code.en: You have {n} first-author papers accepted. Defense preparation takes about three months of thesis writing and slides.
code.zh: 你有 {n} 篇一作论文中稿。准备答辩要写博士论文、做幻灯片，大约得花三个月。

code.en: Recruiting season is open. An internship means 12 weeks of industry research, real compute, and a lot of new people.
code.zh: 招聘季开始了。去实习就是在业界做 12 周研究，卡管够，还能认识一大群新朋友。

code.en: Apply to a couple of places
{company} offers you a summer internship: 12 weeks, starting late May.
code.zh: {company} 给了你暑期实习 offer：12 周，5 月下旬入职。

code.en: Decline and stay in the lab
A fellowship would pay your way for a year, with no TA duty. The research statement takes a couple of days.
code.zh: 拿到奖学金 (fellowship)，一年的开销就有着落了，还不用当助教。写研究陈述得花几天。

code.en: You're close enough to the finish line that people ask what's next. Going on the market takes time, but offers don't arrive on their own.
code.zh: 终点在望，开始有人问你“毕业去哪儿”。找工作很花时间，但 offer 不会自己找上门。

code.en: The degree is done. A few doors are open.
code.zh: 学位到手，眼前有几条路可选。

code.en: After months of applications and interviews, here's what came back.
code.zh: 申请、面试折腾了几个月，结果都在这儿了。

code.en: In your one-on-one, your advisor asks what you're working on next. Right now, the honest answer is “nothing in particular”.
code.zh: 单独会面时，导师问你接下来做什么。老实说，答案是“啥也没在做”。

code.en: You haven't prepared yet. Pass odds: {now} now, {next} if you choose “Prepare for quals” this turn.
code.zh: 你还没开始准备。通过几率：现在{now}，这轮选“准备资格考试”的话{next}。
资格考试倒计时：{weeks} 周

code.en: Your qualifying exam is set for {date}. The committee asks four questions, and two good answers pass.
code.zh: 资格考试定在 {date}。委员会会问四个问题，答好两个就算过。

code.en: Choose “Prepare for quals” on the turns before it to raise your odds.
code.zh: 考前几轮选“准备资格考试”，能提高通过几率。

code.en: Pass odds: {now} now, {one} after one turn of preparing, {two} after two.
code.zh: 通过几率：现在{now}，准备一轮后{one}，准备两轮后{two}。

code.en: Pass odds: {now} now, {one} after one turn of preparing.
code.zh: 通过几率：现在{now}，准备一轮后{one}。

code.en: Leaving isn't losing. Plenty of good lives start here. Where would you go?
code.zh: 离开不等于认输，很多好日子正是从这一步开始的。你想去哪儿？

code.en: You inherit “{title}”, its code, and its mysteries.
code.zh: 你接手了“{title}”，外加一堆代码和代码里的玄学。

code.en: You let this one go. Next target: {deadline}.
Deadline mode. Everything else can wait two weeks.
code.zh: 截稿冲刺模式启动。天大的事也等两周再说。

code.en: You know what to fix. Now you need the days.
code.zh: 你知道该改什么了。现在缺的是时间。

code.en: You write the question on a sticky note and move on.
code.zh: 你把问题写在便利贴上，接着往下做。

code.en: Not every paper is yours to carry.
code.zh: 不是每篇论文都得你来扛。

code.en: A line on your CV you helped earn.
code.zh: 简历上多了一行，也有你的功劳。

code.en: You tell your family. They ask what it means. You explain for twenty minutes.
code.zh: 你把好消息发进家族群。大家问这是啥意思，你解释了二十分钟。

code.en: Findings it is. A publication is a publication.
code.zh: 那就 Findings 吧。蚊子腿也是肉。

code.en: Revision mode. Every reviewer comment is now a to-do item.
code.zh: 进入改稿模式。每条审稿意见都成了待办事项。

code.en: You withdraw it and look for another venue.
You shelve it. It still taught you something.
code.zh: 你把论文搁置了。就当交学费，好歹学到了点东西。

code.en: You go back to the draft and aim for {deadline}.
You present to a camera and a small grid of faces. Two of them ask great questions.
code.zh: 你对着摄像头和一屏九宫格头像做报告。倒是有两位问了很好的问题。

code.en: The travel grant doesn't come through, so you present remotely.
code.zh: 差旅资助没批下来，你只好线上报告。

code.en: Your committee: {names}. The date is set.
code.zh: 你的委员会：{names}。日期定好了。

code.en: Not yet. Your advisor will ask again.
code.zh: 再等等。导师还会再问的。

code.en: Defense prep begins. Thesis chapters, slides, and a date with your committee in about three months.
code.zh: 答辩准备开始了：写博士论文，做幻灯片，大约三个月后还有一场和委员会的约会。

code.en: Thirty applications, one cover letter, many small edits.
code.zh: 海投三十家，一封求职信，改了无数个小细节。

code.en: You sign. Summer will look different this year.
code.zh: 你签了。今年暑假不用在组里过了。

code.en: You stay in the lab for the summer.
code.zh: 这个暑假你留在组里接着搬砖。

code.en: Research statement submitted. Results come in the spring.
code.zh: 研究陈述交上去了，春天出结果。

code.en: You skip the market this year to focus on the thesis.
code.zh: 你今年不找工作，专心写博士论文。

code.en: You polish your CV, your website and your research statement, in that order, several times.
code.zh: 你把简历、个人主页和研究陈述按这个顺序反复打磨了好几遍。

code.en: You accept: {name}. They'll wait until you defend.
code.zh: 你接受了：{name}。对方会等你答辩完。

code.en: You decline and plan to try again next year.
code.zh: 你全都拒了，打算明年再试。

code.en: Your thesis is ready, but you have only {n} first-author papers accepted. The defense happens as soon as the third one lands.
code.zh: 博士论文写好了，但你只有 {n} 篇一作论文中稿。第三篇一中，马上答辩。

code.en: Next academic year is yours: no TA duty, and a line on your CV that people notice.
code.zh: 下一学年归你了：不用当助教，简历上还多了亮眼的一行。

code.en: Fellowship results: not this time. The feedback is polite and mostly about “broader impacts”.
code.zh: 奖学金结果：这次没拿到。反馈很客气，大多在讲“更广泛的影响”。

code.en: Internship season: no offers this year. A few nice rejection emails, and one that called you by someone else's name.
code.zh: 实习季：今年 0 offer。几封客气的拒信，其中一封还叫错了你的名字。

code.en: Your internship at {company} starts. Weekends are still yours.
code.zh: 你在 {company} 的实习开始了。好在周末还是你自己的。

code.en: They offer you a full-time return offer, whenever you're ready.
code.zh: 对方给了你转正 offer，你什么时候准备好都可以来。

code.en: Your internship project turns into a paper you can submit.
code.zh: 实习项目攒成了一篇能投的论文。
你在 {company} 的实习结束了。

code.en: You leave with new friends and better code.
code.zh: 你交到了新朋友，代码也写得更好了。

code.en: Summer in industry · offers in March
code.zh: 暑期去业界 · 3 月出 offer

code.en: A year without TA duty · results in February
code.zh: 一年不用当助教 · 2 月出结果
准备充分 · 通过几率{odds}
通过几率{now} → 再高一点

code.en: About three months · third paper still under review
code.zh: 约三个月 · 第三篇还在审
现在就投 · 春天出 offer

code.en: You send out internship applications: one CV, many small edits.
code.zh: 你投出了实习申请：一份简历，改了无数个小地方。

code.en: Fellowship application submitted. Results come in February.
code.zh: 奖学金申请交上去了，2 月出结果。
开题定好了。你的委员会：{names}。

code.en: Defense preparation begins: thesis chapters, slides, and a date with your committee in about three months.
code.zh: 答辩准备开始：写博士论文，做幻灯片，大约三个月后还有一场和委员会的约会。

code.en: You go on the job market. You polish your CV, your website and your research statement, in that order, several times.
code.zh: 你开始找工作。简历、个人主页、研究陈述，按这个顺序反复打磨了好几遍。

code.en: Reviews are in for “{title}”: {scores} out of 5.
code.zh: “{title}”的审稿意见出来了：{scores}（满分 5 分）。

code.en: {name}'s paper, with you as a co-author, is accepted at {venue}.
code.zh: 你和 {name} 合作的论文中了 {venue}。

code.en: {name}'s paper, with you as a co-author, is rejected. {name} shrugs and starts revising.
code.zh: 你和 {name} 合作的论文被拒了。{name} 耸耸肩，开始改稿。

code.en: Major revision for “{title}” at {venue}. Work on it to address the reviews; it goes back when the revision is done.
code.zh: “{title}”在 {venue} 拿到了大修。继续推进这个项目，按审稿意见修改；改完就会交回去。

code.en: Revise and resubmit for “{title}” at {venue}. Work on it to address the reviews; it goes back when the revision is due.
code.zh: “{title}”在 {venue} 拿到了大修重投 (R&R)。继续推进这个项目，按审稿意见修改；到修改截止时就会交回去。

code.en: You fixed the weakest part of “{title}” before submitting.
code.zh: 投稿前，你补上了“{title}”最薄弱的地方。

code.en: You send the revision of “{title}” back to {venue}.
“{title}” wasn't ready in time. On to the next deadline.
{name} graduated and joined a big tech lab.
code.zh: {name} 毕业了，去了大厂的研究院。

code.en: {name}, your old labmate, joined a big tech lab.
code.zh: 你以前的同门 {name} 去了大厂的研究院。
{name} 毕业了，开启了博后生涯。

code.en: {name}, your old labmate, started a postdoc.
code.zh: 你以前的同门 {name} 开启了博后生涯。

code.en: {name}, your old labmate, founded a startup.
code.zh: 你以前的同门 {name} 出去创业了。

code.en: {name} graduated and took a faculty job.
code.zh: {name} 毕业了，拿到教职，成了青椒。

code.en: {name}, your old labmate, took a faculty job.
code.zh: 你以前的同门 {name} 拿到教职，成了青椒。

code.en: {name} graduated and moved home to teach.
code.zh: {name} 毕业了，回老家教书去了。

code.en: {name}, your old labmate, moved home to teach.
code.zh: 你以前的同门 {name} 回老家教书去了。

code.en: {name} joins the lab as a first-year.
code.zh: 一年级新生 {name} 进组了。

code.en: {title}: the revision is done. Ready to submit.
{title}: it all comes together. Ready to submit.
{title}: the {part} is stronger now, so it should review better.
code.zh: {title}：{part}这块更扎实了，审稿时应该能多拿点分。

code.en: {chance} to finish in a full turn of work

code.zh: {title}：{done}完成了。接下来是{next}（大约 {weeks} 周）。

code.en: Point to what the paper already says. Works when they misread.
code.zh: 指出论文里其实已经写了。对方读错时管用。

code.en: Safe for minor points. You must deliver them in the camera-ready.
code.zh: 小问题这么回很稳妥，但终稿里必须兑现。

code.en: Strong for soundness concerns. Costs 2 days and Energy; results can disappoint.
code.zh: 审稿人质疑方法是否可靠时最有效。要花 2 天和一些精力，结果也可能不如人意。

code.en: Good when they're wrong and open-minded. Risky otherwise.
code.zh: 对方确实错了、又听得进去时好用，否则有风险。

code.en: Satisfying to write. Almost never a good idea.
code.zh: 写着很爽，但几乎总会适得其反。
举报这是 LLM 写的

code.en: Ask the area chair to discount this review. Only offered when a review reads that way.
code.zh: 请领域主席 (AC) 降低这份审稿意见的权重。只有审稿意见读着像 LLM 写的时候才会出现。

code.en: The paper studies an interesting problem.
code.zh: 本文研究了一个有趣的问题。

code.en: You'd already fixed this before submitting. The reply writes itself.
code.zh: 这个你投稿前就改好了。回复信手拈来。
对方扫了一眼你的澄清。

code.en: Clarifying doesn't fix a real problem.
code.zh: 真有问题，澄清也解决不了。

code.en: Nice results, though not quite what they asked.
code.zh: 结果不错，只是跟对方要的不太一样。

code.en: The new baseline beats you. You report it honestly.
code.zh: 新加的 baseline 比你的方法还强。你还是如实报告了。

code.en: The experiment doesn't finish in time.
Your pushback is fair, and they see it.
code.zh: 你的反驳有理，对方也认了。

code.en: They don't enjoy being contradicted on a real issue.
code.zh: 在真问题上被顶回去，对方不太高兴。
对方读出了你的阴阳怪气。

code.en: The area chair agrees this review reads as LLM-written and discounts it.
code.zh: 领域主席也觉得这份审稿意见像 LLM 写的，降低了它的权重。

code.en: The area chair notes your concern.
code.zh: 领域主席记下了你的意见。

code.en: No sign this reviewer read the response.
code.zh: 这位审稿人连“已读”都没给。

code.en: After reading the other reviews, they lower their score.
code.zh: 看完其他审稿意见，对方反手把分降了。

code.en: Two weeks with papers. Projects inch forward; sometimes you get an idea.
code.zh: 花两周读论文。项目会慢慢往前挪，有时还能冒出新想法。

code.en: Sleep in, see friends, or do nothing useful for a while.
code.zh: 睡个懒觉，见见朋友，或者干脆躺平几天。

code.en: Tech hiring is booming. Recruiters are suddenly very friendly.
code.zh: 科技行业招人正火。HR 突然都对你热情得不得了。

code.en: Industry announces hiring freezes. The job boards go quiet.
code.zh: 业界纷纷冻结招聘，求职网站一片冷清。

code.en: The job market settles back to normal.

code.zh: {biglab} 发布了 {model}。一夜之间，人人都在聊{topic}。
{biglab} 发布了 {model}。{topic}一下子凉了半截。

code.en: Shelve this project? You can't bring it back.
code.zh: 确定要搁置这个项目吗？搁置后就没法恢复了。

code.en: Your paper is out for review and nothing else is in progress. Start something new while you wait?
code.zh: 论文在审，手上空了。趁等结果，开个新坑？

code.en: Nothing is in progress right now. Start a new project?
code.zh: 手上没有在推进的项目了。开个新坑？

code.en: Pick one. Keep Energy up, Stress down, Health up.
code.zh: 选一项。让精力高一点，压力低一点，健康好一点。
这个周末要是有空，还可以：

code.en: (optional, on top of your pick below)
code.zh: （选不选都行，不影响下面的主要选择）

code.en: Defense prep can start a year after the proposal.
code.zh: 开题满一年后才能开始准备答辩。

code.en: Doesn’t use the turn. Adds Stress.
code.zh: 不占用本轮时间，但会增加压力。

code.en: {n} out of 5, could rise to {up}, could fall to {down}, counts half if the chair agrees
code.zh: {n} 分（满分 5 分），可能升到 {up} 分，也可能降到 {down} 分，领域主席认可的话只算一半

code.en: {n} out of 5, could rise to {up}, could fall to {down}
code.zh: {n} 分（满分 5 分），可能升到 {up} 分，也可能降到 {down} 分

code.en: {n} out of 5, could rise to {up}, counts half if the chair agrees
code.zh: {n} 分（满分 5 分），可能升到 {up} 分，领域主席认可的话只算一半
{n} 分（满分 5 分），可能升到 {up} 分

code.en: {n} out of 5, could fall to {down}, counts half if the chair agrees
code.zh: {n} 分（满分 5 分），可能降到 {down} 分，领域主席认可的话只算一半
{n} 分（满分 5 分），可能降到 {down} 分

code.en: {n} out of 5, counts half if the chair agrees
code.zh: {n} 分（满分 5 分），领域主席认可的话只算一半

code.en: Pick a reply for each reviewer.
code.zh: 给每位审稿人选一种回复。

code.en: New experiments cost {n} days next turn and some Energy.
code.zh: 补实验要占用下一轮 {n} 天，还要花些精力。

code.en: Two weeks a turn. Run studies, survive Reviewer 2, and see where it leads. Lessons from {phd101}.
code.zh: 两周一轮。跑实验，扛住 2 号审稿人，看看这个博最后读成什么样。干货来自 {phd101}。

code.en: Your browser is blocking storage, so progress won’t be saved if you leave this page.
code.zh: 你的浏览器禁止了本地存储，离开这个页面后进度不会保存。

code.en: Everyone who plays today gets the same traits and the same world: topics, model releases and luck, until your choices diverge.
code.zh: 今天所有玩家的开局都一样：特质、课题、模型发布和运气全都相同，直到你们做出不同的选择。

code.en: Rolled at random. Everyone arrives with something.
code.zh: 开局随机。每个人入学时都自带点什么。

code.en: Everything you have discovered, across every run in this browser.
code.zh: 你在这个浏览器里玩过的所有局，发现过的一切都在这里。

code.en: Your research record (papers, top venues, h-index, citations, letters) against thousands of simulated runs of the game.
code.zh: 拿你的科研成绩（论文、顶会、h 指数、引用、推荐信）和几千局模拟对局比一比。

code.en: From PhD 101, for how you played
code.zh: 来自 PhD 101，按你的玩法挑选
击败了 {n}% 的模拟博士生。
击败了 {n}% 的模拟博士生
读博 {years} 年，一作 1 篇，引用 {citations} 次，被拒 1 次。
读博 {years} 年，一作 1 篇，引用 {citations} 次，被拒 {rejections} 次。
读博 {years} 年，一作 {pubs} 篇，引用 {citations} 次，被拒 1 次。
读博 {years} 年，一作 {pubs} 篇，引用 {citations} 次，被拒 {rejections} 次。
我的读博模拟器结局：{ending}，喜提称号“{title}”。

code.en: The link carries your result, so whoever opens it sees this card. Nothing is stored on the site.
code.zh: 结果就存在链接里，谁打开都能看到这张卡片。网站上什么都不保存。
有人晒出了自己的读博人生

code.en: A game about doing a PhD in NLP and HCI. Play your own.
code.zh: 一款在 NLP 和 HCI 方向读博的小游戏。你的博士，你来读。

endings.en: Tenure-Track Professor
endings.zh: Tenure-Track 青椒

endings.en: Academia
endings.zh: 学术界

endings.en: An assistant professor job: your own lab, and your own grant rejections.
endings.zh: 助理教授职位：有了自己的实验室，也有了自己的基金拒信。

endings.en: You start your own lab. Your first student arrives in September, nervous and brilliant. You catch yourself saying things your advisor used to say, and you mostly mean them.
endings.zh: 你建起了自己的实验室。九月，第一个学生来报到，紧张又聪明。你发现自己活成了导师的样子，嘴里说着导师当年的话，而且大多是真心的。

endings.en: Professor at a Teaching College
endings.zh: 教学型教授

endings.en: A teaching job with small classes and students who come to office hours.
endings.zh: 教学岗：小班授课，学生真的会来答疑。

endings.en: You teach, and you are good at it. Every year a few students find you after class with a question that turns into a project.
endings.zh: 你当了老师，而且教得很好。每年总有几个学生下课后来找你，一个问题聊着聊着就成了一个项目。

endings.en: Postdoc in a Famous Lab
endings.zh: 大牛组博后

endings.en: Two years in a lab everyone has heard of.
endings.zh: 去一个无人不知的实验室待两年。

endings.en: You join a lab whose papers you used to read in reading group. The coffee is better and the deadlines are the same.
endings.zh: 你加入的实验室，正是当年读书会上那些论文的出处。咖啡更好喝了，截稿一个也没少。

endings.en: The Eternal Postdoc
endings.zh: 万年博士后

endings.en: A postdoc, and probably another one after that.
endings.zh: 一份博士后，大概还会有下一份。

endings.en: Your first postdoc becomes your second. You know every visa form by heart and every reviewer by writing style.
endings.zh: 第一段博士后做完，又接上了第二段。签证表格你能倒背如流，审稿人光看文风就知道是谁。

endings.en: Lecturer Across the Pond
endings.zh: 英伦讲师

endings.en: A permanent lectureship overseas, with a new vocabulary for everything.
endings.zh: 海外的长聘讲师职位，什么东西都换了个叫法。

endings.en: You move abroad, learn what "REF" means, and find that most collaborations start at the tea break.
endings.zh: 你搬到国外，搞懂了“REF”是什么意思，还发现大多数合作都是从下午茶开始的。

endings.en: Faculty Back Home
endings.zh: 海归青椒

endings.en: A faculty job in your home country, near family.
endings.zh: 国内的教职，离家近。

endings.en: You go home with a doctorate and a suitcase of ideas. Your parents finally understand your job: you are a professor now.
endings.zh: 你带着博士学位和一箱子想法回了国。爸妈终于说得清你是干什么的了：大学教授。

endings.en: Research Scientist at a Frontier Lab
endings.zh: 算力自由研究员

endings.en: Industry
endings.zh: 工业界

endings.en: A research job at one of the labs everyone is racing.
endings.zh: 去一家人人都想追上的实验室做研究。

endings.en: You join a frontier lab with more compute than you can imagine. Sometimes your name is on a paper the whole field reads.
endings.zh: 你加入了一家前沿 AI 实验室，算力多到你不敢想。时不时地，你的名字会出现在全领域都在读的论文上。

endings.en: Research Scientist at Big Tech
endings.zh: 大厂研究员

endings.en: A research scientist role with a stable team and a nice badge.
endings.zh: 研究员职位：团队稳定，工牌好看。

endings.en: You become a research scientist at a big company. You still publish, but now there's a budget and nobody asks you to TA.
endings.zh: 你成了大厂研究员。论文照发，只是现在有经费了，也没人再让你当助教。

endings.en: Applied Scientist
endings.zh: 应用科学家

endings.en: Build models that real users touch.
endings.zh: 做能真正交到用户手里的模型。

endings.en: Your models ship. Millions of people use something you made, and none of them know your name, which turns out to be fine.
endings.zh: 你的模型上线了。数百万人在用你做的东西，没一个人知道你的名字，而你发现这样也挺好。

endings.en: ML Engineer (with a PhD, for Fun)
endings.zh: 博士码农

endings.en: Good pay, and coworkers who call you Doctor as a joke.
endings.zh: 工资不错，同事总半开玩笑地喊你“博士”。

endings.en: You write code all day and sleep well at night. Sometimes you miss research. Then someone mentions Reviewer 2, and you stop missing it.
endings.zh: 你白天写代码，晚上睡得香。偶尔你也会怀念做研究，直到有人提起 2 号审稿人，你就不怀念了。

endings.en: Quant Researcher
endings.zh: 量化研究员

endings.en: A trading firm wants your statistics skills.
endings.zh: 一家量化基金看上了你的统计功底。

endings.en: You move into finance. The salary is absurd, and your p-values are finally worth money.
endings.zh: 你转行进了金融圈。工资高得离谱，你的 p 值终于值钱了。

endings.en: UX Researcher
endings.zh: UX 研究员

endings.en: Lead user research for AI products.
endings.zh: 主导 AI 产品的用户研究。

endings.en: You spend your days talking to the people who use AI products, which is what your PhD trained you to do best. Product teams start asking for you by name.
endings.zh: 你每天和 AI 产品的用户聊天，这正是读博练出来的看家本领。产品团队开始点名要你。

endings.en: The Return Offer
endings.zh: 实习转正

endings.en: Your internship team wants you back, full time.
endings.zh: 实习时的团队想请你回去，转成全职。

endings.en: You go back to the team from your internship. Your old desk is still there, and so is the sticky note you left on the monitor.
endings.zh: 你回到了实习时的团队。原来的工位还在，你贴在显示器上的便利贴也还在。

endings.en: Founder, Acquired
endings.zh: 创业上岸

endings.en: Startup
endings.zh: 创业

endings.en: You start a company from your thesis. Three stressful years later, a big company buys it. You take a long vacation, then start reading papers again.
endings.zh: 你把博士论文做成了一家公司。焦头烂额了三年，公司被一家大厂收购了。你休了个长假，然后又读起了论文。

endings.en: Founder, Pivoted to B2B SaaS
endings.zh: 创业转型 To B

endings.en: Your startup begins as a research vision and becomes a dashboard for enterprise customers. It pays the bills. You still have the original slide deck.
endings.zh: 你的公司起步时怀揣研究理想，最后成了给企业做数据大屏的。好歹收支打平了。最初那份 PPT 你还留着。

endings.en: Founder, Then Big Tech
endings.zh: 先创业，后大厂

endings.en: Your startup doesn't make it, and you learn more in eighteen months than in five years of grad school. A big lab hires you the week after you close it.
endings.zh: 你的创业公司没撑下来，但这十八个月学到的比读博五年还多。公司关门的第二周，你就被一家大厂的实验室招走了。

endings.en: Start Your Own Company
endings.zh: 自己创业

endings.en: Turn your thesis into a startup. The risk is high and the stories are great.
endings.zh: 把博士论文做成一家创业公司。风险高，故事也精彩。

endings.en: Employee #4 at a Labmate's Startup
endings.zh: 同门公司 4 号员工

endings.en: Your old labmate's startup wants you, and it's offering equity and chaos.
endings.zh: 昔日同门的创业公司想拉你入伙，给股份，也给一地鸡毛。

endings.en: You join your labmate's startup as employee number four. The office is a converted garage and the whiteboard has your old lab's handwriting on it.
endings.zh: 你作为 4 号员工加入了同门的创业公司。办公室是车库改的，白板上还留着你们老实验室的笔迹。

endings.en: Policy Fellow
endings.zh: 政策研究员

endings.en: Other
endings.zh: 其他

endings.en: A fellowship advising on AI policy.
endings.zh: 为 AI 政策出谋划策的研究员职位。

endings.en: You explain language models to people who write the rules. Then you explain them again the next week.
endings.zh: 你给制定规则的人讲解语言模型。到了下周，再讲一遍。

endings.en: Science Journalist
endings.zh: 科学记者

endings.en: Write about AI for people who will never read an arXiv paper.
endings.zh: 写 AI，写给永远不会读 arXiv 的人看。

endings.en: You become the person who explains AI research to the public, carefully, without the hype. Researchers start sending you their preprints.
endings.zh: 你成了给大众讲 AI 研究的人，讲得严谨，从不炒作。研究者们开始主动把预印本发给你。

endings.en: AI YouTuber
endings.zh: AI 科普 UP 主

endings.en: Your paper explainer videos have an audience. Make it a job.
endings.zh: 你的论文解读视频有了观众。干脆转全职吧。

endings.en: Your paper explainers find an audience and a sponsor. The comments are full of grad students thanking you.
endings.zh: 你的论文解读视频有了粉丝，也开始恰饭了。评论区里全是来道谢的研究生。

endings.en: Clinical Informatics at a Hospital
endings.zh: 医院临床信息专家

endings.en: Join a hospital's informatics team and put your work at the bedside.
endings.zh: 加入医院的信息团队，把研究带到病床边。

endings.en: You join the hospital you used to recruit clinicians from. Now you're the one they call when the alerts don't make sense, and you fix them.
endings.zh: 你加入了当年去招募临床医生的那家医院。现在系统警报一不对劲，大家就打电话找你，而你每次都能修好。

endings.en: Master's Out, Happily
endings.zh: 开心转硕

endings.en: Leaving
endings.zh: 换条赛道

endings.en: You leave with a Master's degree and no regrets. The skills come with you, and so do the friends.
endings.zh: 你拿着硕士学位离开，毫无遗憾。学到的本事带得走，朋友也一样。

endings.en: Bubble Tea Shop Owner
endings.zh: 奶茶店老板

endings.en: You open a bubble tea shop near campus. Grad students come in at odd hours, and you always know what they need: half sugar, and someone to say the paper will be fine.
endings.zh: 你在学校附近开了家奶茶店。研究生们总在奇奇怪怪的点儿上门，你也总知道他们要什么：半糖，外加一句“论文会没事的”。

endings.en: Switched Fields
endings.zh: 弃码从医

endings.en: You start medical school. Your classmates are amazed that you already know what an EHR is, and that you have opinions about its interface.
endings.zh: 你进了医学院。同学们惊讶地发现你早就知道电子病历（EHR）是什么，还对它的界面颇有意见。

endings.en: Back to the Family Business
endings.zh: 回家继承家业

endings.en: You go home and join the family business. Within a year you've automated the inventory and your aunt calls you "the scientist".
endings.zh: 你回家接手了家里的生意。不到一年就把库存管理全自动化了，姑姑逢人就叫你“科学家”。

endings.en: The Eternal Student
endings.zh: 万年博士生

endings.en: Year eight ends and the university gently points out the time limit. You leave with a Master's degree and a drawer of almost-finished papers.
endings.zh: 第八年结束时，学校委婉地提醒你：年限到了。你带着硕士学位和一抽屉快写完的论文离开了。

epilogues.en: You and your partner still argue about whose thesis acknowledgments were sweeter.
epilogues.zh: 你和另一半至今还在争，谁的博士论文致谢写得更甜。

epilogues.en: Your cat still sleeps on the keyboard. Some of your best emails were typed by paw.
epilogues.zh: 猫主子还是爱睡在键盘上。你写得最好的几封邮件，有的是它用爪子打的。

epilogues.en: You kept exercising, and your back still works.
epilogues.zh: 你一直坚持锻炼，腰到现在还好使。

epilogues.en: You pulled too many all-nighters in grad school. Now you go to bed at ten.
epilogues.zh: 读博时通宵熬得太多，现在你十点就上床，养生得很。

epilogues.en: Your friends from grad school are still your closest friends.
epilogues.zh: 读博时一起熬过来的那帮人，至今还是你最铁的朋友。

epilogues.en: Your family framed your diploma before you did.
epilogues.zh: 你还没来得及裱，家里人就先把你的学位证书裱起来了。

epilogues.en: You and your advisor still meet for coffee when you're in town.
epilogues.zh: 每次回到那座城市，你还会约导师喝杯咖啡。

epilogues.en: You buy bubble tea for your own team when they come in person, just like your advisor did.
epilogues.zh: 团队来线下开会时，你会给大家买奶茶，就像当年导师对你们那样。

epilogues.en: You notice orphan words everywhere now, even on wedding invitations.
epilogues.zh: 现在你走到哪都能看见独占一行的单词，连婚礼请柬都不放过。

epilogues.en: Your first first-author paper is still the one you're proudest of.
epilogues.zh: 你的第一篇一作论文，至今仍是你最骄傲的一篇。

epilogues.en: You keep a folder of every rejection. It's thicker than your CV.
epilogues.zh: 你把每封拒信都存在一个文件夹里，攒得比简历还厚。

epilogues.en: Somewhere, a first-year is reading your paper in reading group and loving it.
epilogues.zh: 此刻在某个地方，有个博一学生正在读书会上读你的论文，读得津津有味。

epilogues.en: You saw more of the world through conferences than in the rest of your life combined.
epilogues.zh: 你靠开会看到的世界，比这辈子其他时候加起来还多。

epilogues.en: You still play music on weekends, and you're better at it than ever.
epilogues.zh: 你周末还在玩音乐，水平比以前任何时候都高。

epilogues.en: The clinicians you worked with still send you interesting problems.
epilogues.zh: 合作过的临床医生至今还会给你发来有意思的问题。

epilogues.en: You mentor a few students informally. You tell them to close the laptop sometimes.
epilogues.zh: 你私下带着几个学生，常提醒他们：时不时也要合上电脑。

epilogues.en: You learned to say no, which was the hardest skill the PhD taught you.
epilogues.zh: 你学会了说“不”，这是读博教会你最难的一课。

flavor.en: You open final_v3_REAL_final.tex.
flavor.zh: 你打开了 final_v3_REAL_final.tex。

flavor.en: The coffee machine breaks. Lab productivity falls by a third.
flavor.zh: 咖啡机坏了，全组战斗力当场掉了三分之一。

flavor.en: The building's heating is either off or set to Sahara.
flavor.zh: 楼里的暖气只有两档：冰窖和撒哈拉。

flavor.en: Your experiment finishes. It was the wrong config.
flavor.zh: 实验终于跑完了，结果发现配置用错了。

flavor.en: The printer jams the morning of your poster session.
flavor.zh: 海报展示当天早上，打印机准时卡纸。

flavor.en: An undergrad calls you "professor". You don't correct them.
flavor.zh: 有个本科生喊你“教授”。你默默应下了。

flavor.en: You accidentally reply-all to the department list.
flavor.zh: 你手滑点了“全部回复”，邮件发给了全系。原地社死。

flavor.en: Your virtual background slips during a job interview. Your laundry makes a brief appearance.
flavor.zh: 求职面试时虚拟背景突然失灵，晾着的衣服抢了个镜。

flavor.en: The fire alarm goes off during your practice talk.
flavor.zh: 你试讲到一半，火警响了。

flavor.en: A "quick sync" is booked for 90 minutes.
flavor.zh: 说是“简单碰一下”，会议一约就是 90 分钟。

flavor.en: A package update breaks your Python environment.
flavor.zh: 某个包更新了一下，你的 Python 环境原地爆炸。

flavor.en: An hour-long bug turns out to be a typo in a config key.
flavor.zh: 查了一小时的 bug，最后发现是配置里一个键名拼错了。

flavor.en: You find your own paper on a course reading list, described wrongly.
flavor.zh: 你的论文上了某门课的阅读清单，介绍还写错了。

flavor.en: "Can you hear me?" Four times, at the start of every meeting.
flavor.zh: 每次开会，都要先来四遍“能听到吗？”

flavor.en: Your paper gets cited for the opposite of what it says.
flavor.zh: 有人引用了你的论文，引的观点和你写的正好相反。

flavor.en: Orientation week. The new students still believe the GPU queue is a myth.
flavor.zh: 新生入学周。萌新们还以为 GPU 排队只是个传说。

flavor.en: Fall semester starts. The lab fridge still holds three yogurts from last spring.
flavor.zh: 秋季学期开学了。实验室冰箱里还躺着去年春天的三盒酸奶。

flavor.en: Three people at the department Halloween party come dressed as chatbots.
flavor.zh: 系里的万圣节派对上，有三个人 cos 了聊天机器人。

flavor.en: The lab is empty for Thanksgiving week. The GPUs are all yours.
flavor.zh: 感恩节那周，实验室人去楼空。卡全归你了，感恩。

flavor.en: Finals week. The library has no free seats and one working outlet.
flavor.zh: 期末周。图书馆一座难求，能用的插座只有一个。

flavor.en: You grade the same wrong answer 43 times.
flavor.zh: 同一个错误答案，你批改了 43 遍。

flavor.en: Office hours before the midterm. The line reaches the elevator.
flavor.zh: 期中考试前的答疑时间，队伍排到了电梯口。

flavor.en: Winter break. The building is quiet, and the heating has gone home too.
flavor.zh: 寒假。楼里静悄悄的，暖气也放假回家了。

flavor.en: Your out-of-office reply says you're on break. You answer emails anyway.
flavor.zh: 邮件自动回复写着“休假中”，可你照样秒回。

flavor.en: New semester, new to-do list. It looks a lot like the old one.
flavor.zh: 新学期新气象，可待办清单还是老样子。

flavor.en: It's dark by 4:30 pm. Your body clock files a complaint.
flavor.zh: 下午 4:30 天就黑了，生物钟连夜写了篇投诉小作文。

flavor.en: The lab group chat fills with red envelope emojis.
flavor.zh: 实验室群里刷满了红包表情，真红包一个没有。

flavor.en: Spring break. The undergrads leave, and the campus Wi-Fi finally works.
flavor.zh: 春假。本科生都走了，校园 Wi-Fi 终于满血复活。

flavor.en: The trees outside the lab bloom. You admire them through the window.
flavor.zh: 实验室窗外的花开了，你隔着玻璃赏了一会儿。

flavor.en: Regrade requests arrive, all sent after midnight.
flavor.zh: 求改分的邮件陆续到了，全是凌晨发的。

flavor.en: Annual review season. You list your accomplishments, then add some stronger verbs.
flavor.zh: 年度考核季。你列完自己的成果，又把“参与”都改成了“主导”。

flavor.en: Summer starts. The campus is quiet and the parking is easy.
flavor.zh: 夏天到了。校园很安静，车位随便挑。

flavor.en: Half the lab is on internships. Lab meeting is three people and a laptop.
flavor.zh: 组里一半人去实习了，组会就剩三个人加一台笔记本。

flavor.en: The building's AC gives up in the heat wave. The server room is the coolest place on campus.
flavor.zh: 热浪来袭，楼里空调罢工。机房成了全校最凉快的避暑胜地。

flavor.en: The new cohort arrives. They all have better laptops than you.
flavor.zh: 新一届学生来了。人均笔记本都比你的好。

flavor.en: The lab chat gains eleven new members, and eleven new questions about the cluster.
flavor.zh: 实验室群里进了 11 个新人，外加 11 个“集群怎么用”。

flavor.en: Half the lab is coughing. The other half is wearing masks and looking worried.
flavor.zh: 组里一半人在咳嗽，另一半戴着口罩，提心吊胆。

flavor.en: Someone microwaves fish in the lab kitchen again.
flavor.zh: 又有人在实验室茶水间用微波炉热鱼。

flavor.en: Lab meeting runs 40 minutes over. Nobody knows why.
flavor.zh: 组会超时 40 分钟，没人说得清为什么。

flavor.en: The lab fridge has a sign that says "Please label your food". The sign is not labeled.
flavor.zh: 实验室冰箱上贴着“食物请写名字”。这张纸条没写名字。

flavor.en: A labmate brings homemade cookies. Productivity rises briefly, then falls.
flavor.zh: 同门带来自己烤的饼干。全组效率先升后降，标准的倒 U 型曲线。

flavor.en: Someone renames the lab Wi-Fi to "Reviewer2_Is_Watching".
flavor.zh: 有人把实验室 Wi-Fi 改名成了“Reviewer2_Is_Watching”。

flavor.en: The most senior student in the lab tells a deadline story with three morals.
flavor.zh: 组里年级最高的博士生又讲起当年赶 DDL 的故事，附赠三条教训。

flavor.en: You find a comment in the lab codebase that just says "sorry".
flavor.zh: 你在实验室代码库里发现一行注释，只写着“sorry”。

flavor.en: The group chat debates lunch for an hour. Everyone eats at their desk.
flavor.zh: 群里讨论了一小时午饭吃啥。最后全员在工位上吃外卖。

flavor.en: The GPU queue has 412 jobs ahead of yours. You read a paper instead.
flavor.zh: GPU 队列里你前面还排着 412 个任务，你只好先去读篇论文。

flavor.en: Your loss curve goes down smoothly. You don't trust it.
flavor.zh: loss 曲线降得太丝滑了，你反而不敢信。

flavor.en: You spend an hour making a figure colorblind-friendly. It also prints better now.
flavor.zh: 你花了一小时把图改成色盲友好的配色，没想到打印出来也更好看了。

flavor.en: Your random seed is 42, like everyone else's.
flavor.zh: 你的随机种子是 42，和所有人一样。

flavor.en: Your experiment log says "try again tomorrow". It was written three weeks ago.
flavor.zh: 实验日志上写着“明天再试”。落款是三周前。

flavor.en: A bug in your evaluation script makes your results worse and more honest.
flavor.zh: 你在评测脚本里揪出一个 bug。修完之后，结果变差了，也更真实了。

flavor.en: Overleaf reports 37 errors. The PDF looks fine.
flavor.zh: Overleaf 报了 37 个错误。PDF 看着好好的，那就当没错。

flavor.en: You rename a file from results to results_new to results_final to results_final2.
flavor.zh: 你把文件从 results 改名成 results_new，再改成 results_final，再改成 results_final2。

flavor.en: Your notes from last month say "KEY INSIGHT" with nothing after it.
flavor.zh: 上个月的笔记里写着“重大发现：”，后面什么都没写。

flavor.en: The paper you need is behind a paywall. Your university has access, but your VPN doesn't.
flavor.zh: 你要的论文得付费才能看。学校明明买了，可你挂着 VPN 还是打不开。

flavor.en: A tokenizer splits your name into five pieces.
flavor.zh: 分词器把你的名字切成了 5 段。

flavor.en: Your model answers every question with a confident paragraph about penguins.
flavor.zh: 不管问什么，你的模型都一本正经地讲起企鹅。

flavor.en: Your prompt is now longer than your abstract.
flavor.zh: 你的 prompt 已经比论文摘要还长了。

flavor.en: Someone at lab meeting says "just fine-tune it" as if it's one step.
flavor.zh: 组会上有人说“微调一下就行”。把大象装进冰箱还要三步呢。

flavor.en: Your baseline gets better after you fix a bug. Your method doesn't.
flavor.zh: 修完一个 bug，baseline 涨点了，你的方法却纹丝不动。

flavor.en: You read a paper that solves your problem. It's from 1998.
flavor.zh: 你读到一篇论文，正好解决了你的问题。一看年份：1998。

flavor.en: A related-work search for your topic returns your own paper first.
flavor.zh: 你搜相关工作，排第一的是你自己的论文。

flavor.en: Your job crashes at 98%.
flavor.zh: 任务跑到 98% 崩了。当场破防。

flavor.en: Your annotation guidelines are now 14 pages long. Nobody agrees on what counts as "neutral".
flavor.zh: 标注指南已经写到 14 页了，可还是没人说得清什么算“中性”。

flavor.en: Inter-annotator agreement comes back at 0.41. You learn the word "moderate".
flavor.zh: 标注者间一致性算出来是 0.41，你学会了一个体面的说法：“中等一致”。

flavor.en: You compute Cohen's kappa three times and get three different numbers.
flavor.zh: 你算了三遍 Cohen's kappa，得到三个不同的数。

flavor.en: A study participant asks whether the chatbot in your study is a real person.
flavor.zh: 有位参与者问你，研究里的聊天机器人是不是真人。

flavor.en: Your think-aloud participant thinks very quietly.
flavor.zh: 你让参与者出声思考。参与者只思考，不出声。

flavor.en: A participant rates your prototype 7 out of 7, then says they never clicked it.
flavor.zh: 有个参与者给你的原型打了满分 7 分，接着说自己压根没点开过。

flavor.en: A pilot participant finds the bug you hunted all week. It takes them four seconds.
flavor.zh: 你找了一周的 bug，预实验的参与者 4 秒就找到了。

flavor.en: The anchor on your survey scale says "Strongly Disagre". It's been live for a day.
flavor.zh: 量表上的“非常不同意”打成了“非常不同”，可问卷已经上线一天了。

flavor.en: Your interview transcript has 40 instances of "um". Thirty-eight are yours.
flavor.zh: 访谈转录稿里有 40 个“嗯”。其中 38 个是你说的。

flavor.en: The IRB asks you to change "may" to "might" on page 12.
flavor.zh: 伦理审查 (IRB) 要求你把第 12 页的“可能”改成“或许”。

flavor.en: A clinician partner replies to a three-paragraph email with one word: "Thursday?"
flavor.zh: 你给合作的临床医生写了三段话，对方只回了两个字：“周四？”

flavor.en: A participant stays after the session to tell you how to fix your whole interface. They're right.
flavor.zh: 一位参与者结束后没走，教你整个界面该怎么改。你竟无法反驳。

flavor.en: You spend an afternoon choosing between "utilize" and "use". You choose "use".
flavor.zh: 你花了一下午在“utilize”和“use”之间纠结。最后选了“use”。

flavor.en: You now notice orphan words in other people's papers.
flavor.zh: 你开始注意到别人论文里独占一行的单词了。

flavor.en: Your abstract is 251 words. The limit is 250.
flavor.zh: 摘要写了 251 个词，上限是 250。

flavor.en: Your bibliography has the same paper three times, with three different years.
flavor.zh: 你的参考文献里同一篇论文出现了三次，年份还各不相同。

flavor.en: You move a figure up one line. LaTeX moves it two pages down.
flavor.zh: 你把一张图往上挪了一行。LaTeX 反手把它挪到了两页之后。

flavor.en: Your paper title has a colon, like every other title on the reading list.
flavor.zh: 你的论文标题里有个冒号，跟阅读清单上的其他标题一个样。

flavor.en: You write "Interestingly," and then delete it. Then you write it again.
flavor.zh: 你写下“Interestingly,”，删掉，想了想，又写了回去。

flavor.en: Your conference badge spells your name wrong. You answer to it all week.
flavor.zh: 参会胸牌把你的名字拼错了。你将错就错，应了一整周。

flavor.en: The line for coffee is longer than the line for the keynote.
flavor.zh: 买咖啡的队，比听主旨报告的队还长。

flavor.en: You come home with four tote bags and no memory of picking them up.
flavor.zh: 你带回了四个帆布袋，完全不记得是什么时候拿的。

flavor.en: Everyone at your poster asks the same question. You start answering before they finish.
flavor.zh: 来看海报的人都问同一个问题。到后来，对方刚开口你就答完了。

flavor.en: You meet someone whose papers you've cited six times. You forget their name instantly.
flavor.zh: 你见到了一位自己引用过六次的作者，转头就忘了人家叫什么。

flavor.en: Your advisor replies at 12:40 am: "Great figure. No need to reply until Monday."
flavor.zh: 导师凌晨 0:40 回复：“图做得很好。周一之前不用回。”

flavor.en: Your advisor buys bubble tea for everyone who came to lab meeting in person.
flavor.zh: 导师给所有线下来开组会的人点了奶茶。

flavor.en: Your advisor spots an orphan word on page 6 of your draft.
flavor.zh: 导师发现你初稿第 6 页有个单词独占一行。

flavor.en: Your advisor answers your email from a different airport than last week.
flavor.zh: 导师又在机场回了你的邮件，和上周不是同一个机场。

flavor.en: Your advisor schedules a check-in about your check-in.
flavor.zh: 导师约你开个会，聊聊你们开会的事。

flavor.en: Your advisor has a new grant and, with it, a new spreadsheet.
flavor.zh: 导师拿到一笔新经费，附赠一张新表格。

flavor.en: Your advisor pitches a startup idea over lunch. It's the third one this month.
flavor.zh: 导师午饭时又讲了个创业点子，这个月已经第三个了。

flavor.en: Your advisor asks whether your p-value survived the correction.
flavor.zh: 导师问你，p 值做完校正还挺得住吗。

flavor.en: Your advisor tells a story from 1994 that turns out to be exactly relevant.
flavor.zh: 导师讲起 1994 年的往事，没想到正好切题。

flavor.en: Your advisor sketches a ten-year research vision on a napkin.
flavor.zh: 导师在餐巾纸上画出了未来十年的研究蓝图。

flavor.en: Your advisor sends you a paper at 6 am with the subject line "!!".
flavor.zh: 导师早上 6 点给你发了一篇论文，邮件主题只有“！！”。

flavor.en: Your advisor apologizes that the travel budget is, once again, mostly hope.
flavor.zh: 导师一脸歉意地说，这次的差旅经费又只能靠爱发电了。

flavor.en: Your advisor forwards a message from the company side with one word: "thoughts?"
flavor.zh: 导师转发了一条公司那边的消息，只附了一句：“怎么看？”

flavor.en: Your cat sits on the exact paragraph you're reading.
flavor.zh: 猫一屁股坐在你正在读的那一段上。

flavor.en: Your cat knocks your coffee off the desk, then looks at you.
flavor.zh: 猫把你的咖啡从桌上推了下去，然后静静地看着你。

flavor.en: The lab whiteboard still has equations from 2019. Nobody dares erase them.
flavor.zh: 实验室白板上还留着 2019 年的公式。祖传的，没人敢擦。

flavor.en: Your citation profile gets merged with someone who has a similar name. You now have three papers on dairy cattle.
flavor.zh: 你的学术主页和一个名字差不多的人合并了，于是你喜提三篇奶牛研究论文。

flavor.en: A squirrel outside the window becomes the lab mascot. It now has its own channel in the lab chat.
flavor.zh: 窗外的一只松鼠成了实验室吉祥物，现在还有了自己的专属群聊。

flavor.en: The vending machine eats your last dollar. The granola bar hangs there, just out of reach.
flavor.zh: 自动售货机吞了你最后一块钱。燕麦棒卡在半空，近在咫尺，远在天涯。

flavor.en: You name your model after a faction from your favorite sci-fi novel. The reviewers don't get the reference.
flavor.zh: 你用最喜欢的科幻小说里的一个派系给模型起名，可惜审稿人没 get 到。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor's out-of-office reply has its own out-of-office reply.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师的自动回复，居然也设了自动回复。

flavor_advisor.en: You catch your advisor on a conference livestream. It's the longest you've seen them this month.
flavor_advisor.zh: 你在会议直播里刷到了导师，这是这个月你见导师最久的一次。

flavor_advisor.en: A calendar invite arrives: "Sync about the sync."
flavor_advisor.zh: 收到一个会议邀请：“关于对齐会的对齐会。”

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor leaves a comment on your comment.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师在你的批注上又加了一条批注。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor's whiteboard says "Papers this year: 9", and it's only October.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师的白板上写着“今年论文：9 篇”，而现在才十月。

flavor_advisor.en: The lab's one GPU has a sign-up sheet taped to it. Your advisor always signs up last.
flavor_advisor.zh: 实验室唯一的一张卡上贴着预约表，导师每次都把自己排在最后。

flavor_advisor.en: Every slide at lab meeting now has an Aim number in the corner.
flavor_advisor.zh: 现在组会上的每页 PPT，角上都标着基金的 Aim 编号。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor's new idea arrived at 2 am. By 9 am it had a sequel.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师的新想法凌晨 2 点到货。到早上 9 点，已经出了续集。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor joins lab meeting from a company building, in front of a ping-pong table.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师从公司大楼连线组会，身后一张乒乓球桌，大厂味扑面而来。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor starts a sentence with "Back in 1994". You take notes.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师一开口就是“想当年，1994 年……”。你赶紧掏出笔记本。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor's email signature lists four companies. One is new this week.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师的邮件签名里挂着四家公司，其中一家是这周新挂上的。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor writes "n = ?" in the margin of your vacation request.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师在你的请假条旁边批注：“n = ?”

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor replies at 1:12 am: "Great figure."
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师凌晨 1:12 回复：“图做得很好。”

flavor_advisor.en: You now notice orphan words in other people's papers.
flavor_advisor.zh: 你开始注意到别人论文里独占一行的单词了。

flavor_advisor.en: Lab meeting bubble tea arrives. Yours is already labeled.
flavor_advisor.zh: 组会奶茶到了，你那杯上已经写好了名字。

flavor_advisor.en: Your advisor fixes the capitalization in your email's subject line.
flavor_advisor.zh: 导师帮你改了邮件标题的大小写。

flavor_advisor.en: A comment on your draft asks "Who cares?", followed by a small smiley face.
flavor_advisor.zh: 初稿上有一条批注：“谁在乎？”后面还画了个小笑脸。

opportunities.en: Go home for the holidays
opportunities.zh: 回家过节

opportunities.en: The holidays are here. Everyone else is leaving campus.
opportunities.zh: 放假了，大家都在陆续离校。

opportunities.en: You eat home cooking and see old friends. Only one relative asks about your h-index.
opportunities.zh: 你吃上了家里的饭，见了老朋友。七大姑八大姨里，只有一位问了你的 h 指数。

opportunities.en: Take the winter break off
opportunities.zh: 寒假好好歇一歇

opportunities.en: Winter break. The lab is empty and the inbox is quiet.
opportunities.zh: 寒假到了，实验室空荡荡的，收件箱也难得安静。

opportunities.en: You take a real break and start the new year with a clear head.
opportunities.zh: 你实打实地歇了一回，满血迎接新的一年。

opportunities.en: Celebrate Lunar New Year
opportunities.zh: 过春节

opportunities.en: Lunar New Year is here, and the family group chat is busy.
opportunities.zh: 春节到了，家族群里的红包和拜年表情刷了屏。

opportunities.en: You eat too many dumplings and call everyone back home.
opportunities.zh: 你饺子吃撑了，还挨个给家里人打电话拜了年。

opportunities.en: Take a spring break trip
opportunities.zh: 春假出去玩

opportunities.en: Spring break. Friends are planning a trip somewhere warm.
opportunities.zh: 春假到了，朋友们正商量着去个暖和的地方玩。

opportunities.en: You spend a week in the sun without reading a single paper.
opportunities.zh: 你晒了一周太阳，一篇论文都没读。

opportunities.en: Take a real vacation
opportunities.zh: 好好度个假

opportunities.en: It's summer, and you haven't taken more than a weekend off in a long time.
opportunities.zh: 夏天到了，你已经很久没休过超过一个周末的假了。

opportunities.en: Two weeks without a laptop. It feels strange for two days, then wonderful.
opportunities.zh: 两周不碰电脑。前两天浑身不自在，之后爽到飞起。

opportunities.en: Go to a summer school
opportunities.zh: 参加暑期学校

opportunities.en: A summer school on human-centered NLP has a spot for you.
opportunities.zh: 一个以人为中心的 NLP 暑期学校给你留了个名额。

opportunities.en: You hear lectures from people whose papers you've read and join a group chat that lasts for years.
opportunities.zh: 好多只在论文里见过的名字，这回亲自给你上课。你还进了一个一聊就是好几年的群。

opportunities.en: Join a hackathon
opportunities.zh: 参加黑客马拉松

opportunities.en: A week-long hackathon on AI for health is looking for teammates.
opportunities.zh: 一场为期一周的 AI 医疗黑客马拉松在招队友。

opportunities.en: You barely sleep for a week. The demo works, and three teammates want to keep going.
opportunities.zh: 你一周几乎没睡。demo 跑通了，三个队友还想接着做下去。

opportunities.en: Join the writing retreat for “{project}”
opportunities.zh: 带“{project}”去闭关写作

opportunities.en: The department's writing retreat has a seat open, in a quiet room with no meetings.
opportunities.zh: 系里的闭关写作营还有个空位，房间安静，一个会都没有。

opportunities.en: Five quiet days later, the draft has grown more than it did all month.
opportunities.zh: 安安静静写了五天，初稿的进度比之前一整个月还多。

opportunities.en: Run everything on the empty GPU cluster
opportunities.zh: 把实验全扔上空闲的 GPU 集群

opportunities.en: Everyone else is at a conference. The GPU cluster is completely empty.
opportunities.zh: 别人都去开会了，集群上的卡全空着。

opportunities.en: With no queue, you run a month of experiments in a week.
opportunities.zh: 不用排队，你一周跑完了一个月的实验。

opportunities.en: Run study sessions while the clinic has openings
opportunities.zh: 趁诊所有空档集中做研究

opportunities.en: The clinic suddenly has two weeks of open slots for your study.
opportunities.zh: 诊所突然空出两周的时段，正好可以做你的研究。

opportunities.en: You run back-to-back sessions, and the clinicians all show up.
opportunities.zh: 你一场接一场地排，临床医生们居然全都到了。

opportunities.en: Work side by side with your advisor
opportunities.zh: 和导师并肩干活

opportunities.en: Your advisor's calendar is unexpectedly free for the next two weeks.
opportunities.zh: 导师接下来两周的日程居然是空的。

opportunities.en: You spend two weeks at the whiteboard with your advisor and learn how they think.
opportunities.zh: 你和导师在白板前泡了两周，总算摸清了导师是怎么想问题的。

opportunities.en: Visit a collaborator's lab for two weeks
opportunities.zh: 去合作者的实验室访问两周

opportunities.en: A collaborator invites you to spend two weeks in their lab.
opportunities.zh: 一位合作者邀请你去对方的实验室待两周。

opportunities.en: Their lab does things differently, and they spot problems you had stopped seeing.
opportunities.zh: 那边做事的方式不一样，一眼就看出了你早就习以为常的问题。

opportunities.en: Help {labmate} make their deadline
opportunities.zh: 帮 {labmate} 赶截稿

opportunities.en: {labmate} has a deadline Friday and is drowning.
opportunities.zh: {labmate} 周五截稿，已经焦头烂额。

opportunities.en: You fix the plots and rewrite the related work. They promise to return the favor.
opportunities.zh: 你修好了图，重写了相关工作。对方说以后一定还你这个人情。

opportunities.en: Take an undergrad under your wing
opportunities.zh: 带一个本科生

opportunities.en: An eager undergrad wants to do research and your advisor suggests you.
opportunities.zh: 一个积极的本科生想做科研，导师让对方来找你。

opportunities.en: You spend two weeks setting them up, and explaining your work helps you understand it better.
opportunities.zh: 你花了两周带对方上手，给别人讲自己的工作，反倒让你理解得更透了。

opportunities.en: Prepare for the career fair
opportunities.zh: 备战招聘会

opportunities.en: The fall career fair is next week. Recruiters from big labs will be there.
opportunities.zh: 秋季招聘会下周开始，各大厂实验室都会来招人。

opportunities.en: You polish your CV and pitch, and come home with a tote bag of stickers.
opportunities.zh: 你打磨好了简历和自我介绍，最后拎回来一帆布袋贴纸。

opportunities.en: Give an invited talk at another university
opportunities.zh: 去外校做特邀报告

opportunities.en: A professor who read your paper invites you to give a talk.
opportunities.zh: 一位读过你论文的教授邀请你去做报告。

opportunities.en: Your talk goes well, and the hard questions come from people who actually read the paper.
opportunities.zh: 报告很顺利，刁钻的问题都来自真正读过论文的人。

opportunities.en: Run a reading sprint with the lab
opportunities.zh: 和组里来一场读论文冲刺

opportunities.en: The lab wants to read the ten most important papers of the year, together, over the next two weeks.
opportunities.zh: 组里想在接下来两周一起读完今年最重要的十篇论文。

opportunities.en: Ten papers and five arguments later, the lab roughly agrees on where the field is going.
opportunities.zh: 十篇论文、五次争论之后，组里对领域的走向大致达成了共识。

opportunities.en: Teach the next two weeks of lectures
opportunities.zh: 代上接下来两周的课

opportunities.en: The professor you TA for is traveling and asks you to teach.
opportunities.zh: 你当助教的那门课，教授要出差，请你代课。

opportunities.en: You give three lectures, and your slides improve each time.
opportunities.zh: 你讲了三次课，PPT 一次比一次好。

opportunities.en: Host prospective students at visit day
opportunities.zh: 在开放日接待来访学生

opportunities.en: Visit day is coming. Your advisor asks you to show prospective students around.
opportunities.zh: 开放日快到了。导师让你带来访的申请者们四处转转。

opportunities.en: You hear yourself giving the advice you needed in your first year.
opportunities.zh: 你听见自己说出了一年级时最需要听到的建议。

opportunities.en: Take two quiet weeks
opportunities.zh: 安安静静歇两周

opportunities.en: You've been running on empty. Your advisor tells you to take some time.
opportunities.zh: 你一直在硬撑，导师让你先歇一阵子。

opportunities.en: Nothing urgent turns out to be urgent. You come back steadier.
opportunities.zh: 结果发现，那些急事其实都不急。回来时你的状态稳多了。

opportunities.en: Join the thesis-writing bootcamp
opportunities.zh: 参加博士论文写作营

opportunities.en: The graduate school runs a week-long thesis bootcamp.
opportunities.zh: 研究生院办了个为期一周的论文写作营。

opportunities.en: You write eight hours a day next to people doing the same. By Friday you have a chapter.
opportunities.zh: 你和一群论文搭子并排坐着，每天写八小时。到周五，你写完了一章。

qa.en: Tell us about the classic paper on your list that everyone cites and nobody reads. What did it actually claim?
qa.zh: 说说你阅读清单上那篇人人都引、没人真读过的经典论文。它到底讲了什么？

qa.en: Why does self-attention get so expensive on long inputs, and what do people do about it?
qa.zh: 输入一长，自注意力的开销为什么就那么大？大家一般怎么解决？

qa.en: What do word-overlap metrics like BLEU actually measure, and when do they disagree with people?
qa.zh: BLEU 这类词重叠指标到底在衡量什么？什么时候会和人工评价对不上？

qa.en: Can you average Likert responses and run a t-test on them? Defend your answer.
qa.zh: 李克特量表的数据能直接取平均做 t 检验吗？说说理由。

qa.en: When would you choose a within-subjects design over a between-subjects one?
qa.zh: 什么情况下你会选被试内设计，而不是被试间设计？

qa.en: Explain subword tokenization. What goes wrong for languages it wasn't built for?
qa.zh: 解释一下子词切分。遇到设计时没考虑到的语言，会出什么问题？

qa.en: Your annotators reach a kappa of 0.4. Is that good? Who gets to decide?
qa.zh: 标注员之间的 kappa 是 0.4。这算好吗？谁说了算？

qa.en: If the whole field tunes on the same benchmark for five years, what are we actually measuring?
qa.zh: 如果整个领域五年都在同一个基准上调参，我们到底在衡量什么？

qa.en: Your reading list is almost all NLP. What do you know about how HCI evaluates systems?
qa.zh: 你的阅读清单几乎全是 NLP。那 HCI 是怎么评估系统的，你了解多少？

qa.en: What can a think-aloud study tell you that a usage log cannot?
qa.zh: 出声思考研究能告诉你哪些使用日志看不出来的东西？

qa.en: Ten years from now, which part of today's NLP will look naive?
qa.zh: 十年后回头看，今天 NLP 的哪部分会显得很天真？

qa.en: Does a model that predicts the next word understand anything? Yes or no.
qa.zh: 一个预测下一个词的模型，真的理解了什么吗？只能回答是或否。

qa.en: Explain how models are tuned with human preference feedback, and one way it can go wrong.
qa.zh: 解释一下怎么用人类偏好反馈来调模型，再说一种可能出问题的情况。

qa.en: What exactly does a p-value of 0.04 tell you? And what doesn't it tell you?
qa.zh: p 值等于 0.04，到底说明了什么？又说明不了什么？

qa.en: Name two ways the wording of a survey question can bias the answer.
qa.zh: 问卷题目的措辞会怎样带偏回答？举两个例子。

qa.en: Which paper on your reading list do you disagree with most, and why?
qa.zh: 阅读清单上你最不认同哪篇论文？为什么？

qa.en: You've read 80 papers. Which open problem in them do you think nobody is working on?
qa.zh: 你读了 80 篇论文，你觉得里面哪个开放问题还没人在做？

qa.en: Why is this a PhD and not a product?
qa.zh: 为什么这是博士课题，而不是一个产品？

qa.en: State your research question in one sentence. Now say it again without the word "LLM".
qa.zh: 用一句话说出你的研究问题。现在再说一遍，不许用“LLM”这个词。

qa.en: Who exactly benefits if this works, and have you asked them?
qa.zh: 如果这个做成了，到底谁会受益？你问过他们吗？

qa.en: This looks like three PhDs. Which part would you cut?
qa.zh: 这工作量够读三个博士了。你打算砍掉哪部分？

qa.en: Your timeline assumes IRB approval in four weeks. What happens if it takes twelve?
qa.zh: 你的时间安排默认伦理审查 (IRB) 4 周就能批下来。要是拖到 12 周呢？

qa.en: Twelve clinicians. How do you know that's enough?
qa.zh: 12 位临床医生，你怎么确定这就够了？

qa.en: What's the strongest baseline you are not planning to compare against?
qa.zh: 你没打算比较的 baseline 里，最强的是哪个？

qa.en: If next year's model solves your task zero-shot, what is left of this thesis?
qa.zh: 如果明年的模型零样本就能解决你的任务，这篇博士论文还剩下什么？

qa.en: How do your three studies connect? Draw it for us.
qa.zh: 你的三项研究是怎么串起来的？画给我们看。

qa.en: How will you know your system helps people, beyond scoring well on a benchmark?
qa.zh: 除了在基准上分数好看，你怎么知道你的系统真的帮到了人？

qa.en: Does this scale?
qa.zh: 这能规模化吗？

qa.en: What could go wrong for a participant in your study, and how will you prevent it?
qa.zh: 你的研究可能给参与者带来什么风险？你打算怎么预防？

qa.en: Last year there were a dozen papers on LLM explanations for clinicians. How is yours different?
qa.zh: 去年光是给临床医生做 LLM 解释的论文就有十几篇。你的创新点在哪？

qa.en: Your plan depends on hospital data you don't have yet. What's plan B?
qa.zh: 你的计划要靠还没拿到的医院数据。B 计划是什么？

qa.en: What is the theoretical contribution here, beyond "we built it and people liked it"?
qa.zh: 除了“我们做了个东西，大家觉得不错”，这里的理论贡献是什么？

qa.en: Who annotates your data, and how will you know they agree for the right reasons?
qa.zh: 谁来标注你的数据？他们意见一致，你怎么确定是出于对的理由？

qa.en: In one sentence: what does the field know now that it didn't before your thesis?
qa.zh: 一句话：有了你的论文，这个领域多知道了什么？

qa.en: If you started your PhD again today, what would you do differently?
qa.zh: 如果今天让你从头再读一次博，你会做哪些不一样的选择？

qa.en: What is the biggest limitation of your thesis that no reviewer caught?
qa.zh: 你的论文最大的局限是什么？审稿人都没发现的那种。

qa.en: All your studies were in one hospital system. Why should anyone believe this generalizes?
qa.zh: 你所有的研究都是在同一个医院系统里做的。凭什么让人相信结论能推广？

qa.en: In Chapter 3 you ran 14 tests on 20 participants. Did you correct for multiple comparisons?
qa.zh: 第 3 章你在 20 位参与者身上做了 14 次检验。做多重比较校正了吗？

qa.en: Chapter 2 says users want more explanation. Chapter 4 says they ignored it. Which is it?
qa.zh: 第 2 章说用户想要更多解释，第 4 章说他们根本没看。到底哪个对？

qa.en: You used an LLM to grade your outputs. Who graded the grader?
qa.zh: 你用 LLM 给输出打分。那谁来给这个评委打分？

qa.en: Walk us through how your annotation guidelines changed between version 1 and the final version.
qa.zh: 带我们过一遍：你的标注指南从第 1 版到最终版是怎么变的？

qa.en: Could you explain Figure 5 again? Slowly, this time.
qa.zh: 能再解释一遍图 5 吗？这次慢一点。

qa.en: What is the first paper someone should write after reading your thesis?
qa.zh: 读完你的论文，别人接下来该写的第一篇论文是什么？

qa.en: Which result surprised you most, and did you believe it at first?
qa.zh: 哪个结果最让你意外？你一开始信了吗？

qa.en: Could a new student reproduce your main result from the code you released?
qa.zh: 一个新生能用你公开的代码复现主要结果吗？

qa.en: Your title says "trustworthy". Did you measure trust, or did you ask people whether they trusted it?
qa.zh: 你的标题里写着“可信”。你是真的测量了信任，还是只问了大家信不信？

qa.en: Your main results use a model behind an API that has changed since. Are your numbers still valid?
qa.zh: 你的主要结果依赖一个 API 模型，可它后来已经更新了。这些数字还作数吗？

qa.en: Is this an NLP thesis or an HCI thesis? Pick one.
qa.zh: 这是 NLP 论文还是 HCI 论文？选一个。

qa.en: What will your lab be working on five years from now?
qa.zh: 五年后你的实验室会在做什么？

qa.en: Who would fund this work, and what is your first grant proposal about?
qa.zh: 谁会资助这项研究？你的第一份基金申请打算写什么？

qa.en: What course would you teach here that we don't already offer?
qa.zh: 如果来我们这儿，你会开一门什么新课？

qa.en: Industry labs have a thousand times your compute. Why do this research at a university?
qa.zh: 工业界实验室的算力是你的一千倍。为什么还要在高校做这个研究？

qa.en: How is your research agenda different from your advisor's?
qa.zh: 你的研究方向和导师的有什么不同？

qa.en: Who in this department would you collaborate with first, and on what?
qa.zh: 来了以后，你会先找系里哪位老师合作？做什么？

qa.en: How would you mentor a student who wants to work on something you don't know well?
qa.zh: 如果学生想做你不太熟悉的方向，你会怎么带？

qa.en: Most of your citations come from one paper. What is your second act?
qa.zh: 你的引用大部分来自同一篇论文。下一篇代表作在哪？

qa.en: Has anyone actually used your system outside a study?
qa.zh: 研究之外，真有人用过你的系统吗？

qa.en: How would you evaluate an AI feature before it ships to millions of users?
qa.zh: 一个 AI 功能上线给几百万用户之前，你会怎么评估它？

qa.en: Your topic is hot right now. What happens to your agenda when it cools down?
qa.zh: 你的方向现在很火。等风口过了，你的研究规划怎么办？

qa.en: Why do you want to be here, specifically?
qa.zh: 说具体点，你为什么想来我们这儿？

qa.en: Your system is mostly prompts. What is the engineering contribution?
qa.zh: 你的系统主要是一堆 prompt。工程贡献在哪？

qa.en: If we made you an offer and so did a big tech company, which would you take? Be honest.
qa.zh: 如果我们给你 offer，大厂也给了，你选哪个？说实话。

qa.en: Tell us about a time a class you taught went badly. What did you change?
qa.zh: 讲讲你哪次上课上砸了，后来改了什么？

qa.en: asks about statistics
qa.zh: 专问统计

qa.en: the industry external member who asks about scalability
qa.zh: 来自业界的外部委员，专问能不能规模化

qa.en: always 20 minutes late
qa.zh: 永远迟到 20 分钟

qa.en: secretly your biggest fan
qa.zh: 其实是你的隐藏铁粉

qa.en: the theory person
qa.zh: 搞理论的那位

qa.en: the clinician collaborator
qa.zh: 合作的临床医生

qa.en: asks how you coded your interviews
qa.zh: 专问你访谈是怎么编码的

qa.en: remembers when all of this was n-grams
qa.zh: 经历过 n-gram 时代的老前辈

qa.en: plays devil's advocate on purpose
qa.zh: 故意唱反调

qa.en: has read every paper you cite, and one you didn't
qa.zh: 读过你引的每一篇，外加一篇你没引的

qa.en: silent for an hour, then asks the hardest question
qa.zh: 沉默一小时，一开口就是最难的问题

qa.en: asks what it all means
qa.zh: 总问“这有什么意义”

recommendations.en: You burned out at least once.
recommendations.zh: 你至少倦怠过一次。

recommendations.en: You spent a lot of weekends working.
recommendations.zh: 你不少周末都在加班。

recommendations.en: You rarely took real breaks.
recommendations.zh: 你很少好好休息。

recommendations.en: Your health took a hit.
recommendations.zh: 你的健康受了影响。

recommendations.en: You left before the finish line.
recommendations.zh: 你没走到终点就离开了。

recommendations.en: What the PhD gives you, even without the degree.
recommendations.zh: 就算没拿到学位，读博也给了你这些。

recommendations.en: You collected a lot of rejections.
recommendations.zh: 你攒了不少拒稿。

recommendations.en: Your Stress ran high along the way.
recommendations.zh: 这一路上，你的压力一直不小。

recommendations.en: A paper went out before it was ready.
recommendations.zh: 有篇论文还没准备好就投出去了。

recommendations.en: Your rebuttals made promises you had to keep.
recommendations.zh: 你在 rebuttal 里许下的承诺，后来都得兑现。

recommendations.en: Writing was your weakest skill.
recommendations.zh: 写作是你最大的短板。

recommendations.en: Your writing could have been clearer.
recommendations.zh: 你的文字本可以更清楚。

recommendations.en: You didn't read much outside your projects.
recommendations.zh: 项目之外的论文，你读得不多。

recommendations.en: Getting scooped often starts with a missed paper.
recommendations.zh: 被撞车，往往是从漏读一篇论文开始的。

recommendations.en: Your advisor relationship could have been stronger.
recommendations.zh: 你和导师的关系本可以更好。

recommendations.en: Novelty was a recurring problem.
recommendations.zh: 创新性屡次被质疑。

recommendations.en: You ran human-centered studies.
recommendations.zh: 你做过以人为中心的研究。

recommendations.en: Make sure the direction becomes yours.
recommendations.zh: 要让这个方向真正成为你自己的。

recommendations.en: Research has no answers in the back of the book.
recommendations.zh: 做研究，可没有书后的参考答案。

recommendations.en: Why research, after all?
recommendations.zh: 说到底，为什么要做研究？

recommendations.en: A checklist for your next project.
recommendations.zh: 下一个项目开工前的检查清单。

recommendations.en: Every project starts with one sentence.
recommendations.zh: 每个项目都从一句话开始。

recommendations.en: From the gap to the method.
recommendations.zh: 从研究空白到方法。

recommendations.en: From numbers to findings.
recommendations.zh: 从数字到发现。

recommendations.en: Where your work should go next.
recommendations.zh: 你的工作下一步该投向哪里。

recommendations.en: What keeps you going after the citations.
recommendations.zh: 引用之外，是什么让你坚持下去。

recommendations.en: How to pick up new methods faster.
recommendations.zh: 怎样更快学会新方法。

recommendations.en: Teach yourself from the papers you admire.
recommendations.zh: 从你佩服的论文里自学。

reviews.en: The Expert
reviews.zh: 小同行

reviews.en: I have worked on closely related problems, so I read this paper carefully, appendix included.
reviews.zh: 本人长期从事相关方向研究，认真通读了全文（含附录）。

reviews.en: This paper tackles a real problem in {topic}, and most of my concerns can be fixed.
reviews.zh: 本文针对{topic}中的真实问题，具有一定研究意义，我的大部分疑虑可通过修改解决。

reviews.en: The paper is technically solid. My questions are mostly about scope and framing.
reviews.zh: 本文技术路线扎实，我的问题主要集中在研究范围和叙事框架上。

reviews.en: I checked the main results against the released code, and they match.
reviews.zh: 我用作者公开的代码核对了主要结果，二者一致。

reviews.en: The Skimmer
reviews.zh: 摘要党

reviews.en: The paper proposes something about {topic}. I did not have time to read the appendix.
reviews.zh: 本文就{topic}提出了某种东西。由于时间有限，未能阅读附录。

reviews.en: Confidence: 2. This is not my main area, but the idea seems reasonable.
reviews.zh: 置信度：2。本人并非该方向专家，但想法看起来合理。

reviews.en: Overall the paper is fine, though I may have missed some details.
reviews.zh: 总体而言本文尚可，不过我可能遗漏了一些细节。

reviews.en: I read the abstract, the figures and the conclusion carefully.
reviews.zh: 我仔细阅读了摘要、图表和结论。

reviews.en: Reviewer 2
reviews.zh: 2 号审稿人

reviews.en: The authors propose yet another approach to {topic}.
reviews.zh: 作者针对{topic}又提出了一种方法。

reviews.en: The paper is well written and easy to follow. Unfortunately, I have serious concerns.
reviews.zh: 本文写作清晰，易于理解。遗憾的是，我有一些严重的疑虑。

reviews.en: I struggle to see what this paper adds to the literature.
reviews.zh: 我很难看出本文相对现有工作有什么新的贡献。

reviews.en: I have several major concerns, listed in no particular order, since they are all major.
reviews.zh: 我有若干重大问题，排名不分先后，因为它们都很重大。

reviews.en: The Champion
reviews.zh: 真爱粉

reviews.en: This is one of the best papers in my batch, and I would like to see it at {venue}.
reviews.zh: 这是我这批稿件中最好的论文之一，希望能在 {venue} 上看到它。

reviews.en: I enjoyed reading this paper and learned something from it.
reviews.zh: 读这篇论文是一种享受，我从中有所收获。

reviews.en: This paper asks exactly the question the field should be asking about {topic}.
reviews.zh: 本文针对{topic}提出的，正是这个领域应该追问的问题。

reviews.en: The Citation Seeker
reviews.zh: 引用推销员

reviews.en: The paper overlooks an important line of prior work.
reviews.zh: 本文忽视了一个重要的已有研究方向。

reviews.en: The idea is interesting, but it is closely related to {fake_prior}, which is not discussed.
reviews.zh: 想法很有趣，但与 {fake_prior} 密切相关，而文中并未讨论。

reviews.en: The related work section is incomplete in ways that matter.
reviews.zh: 相关工作部分存在关键性的遗漏。

reviews.en: The Scope Police
reviews.zh: 会场保安

reviews.en: This is a solid paper, but I am not convinced it belongs at {venue}.
reviews.zh: 这是一篇扎实的论文，但我不确定它适合 {venue}。

reviews.en: This reads more like an HCI paper than an NLP paper.
reviews.zh: 本文读起来更像 HCI 论文，而非 NLP 论文。

reviews.en: This reads more like an NLP paper than an HCI paper.
reviews.zh: 本文读起来更像 NLP 论文，而非 HCI 论文。

reviews.en: The work may find a more appreciative audience at a domain-specific venue.
reviews.zh: 这项工作若投到更对口的专业会议或期刊，或许能遇到更赏识它的读者。

reviews.en: The Baseline Hunter
reviews.zh: baseline 猎手

reviews.en: The idea is interesting, but the experimental comparison is incomplete.
reviews.zh: 想法很有趣，但实验对比不够完整。

reviews.en: Why not simply use {model}?
reviews.zh: 为什么不直接用 {model}？

reviews.en: The baselines in the main table are not the strongest available.
reviews.zh: 主表中的 baseline 并非目前最强的。

reviews.en: The LLM-Written Review
reviews.zh: AI 味审稿意见

reviews.en: This paper delves into the intricate landscape of {topic}, offering a comprehensive exploration.
reviews.zh: 本文深入探讨了{topic}这一错综复杂的领域，进行了全面而系统的探索。

reviews.en: Strengths: The paper is well-written. Weaknesses: The paper could be improved.
reviews.zh: 优点：本文写作良好。缺点：本文仍有改进空间。

reviews.en: In the ever-evolving field of {topic}, this paper presents a novel and timely contribution.
reviews.zh: 在日新月异、蓬勃发展的{topic}领域，本文做出了新颖且及时的贡献。

reviews.en: Overall, this paper makes a valuable contribution, but there are several areas for improvement.
reviews.zh: 总的来说，本文做出了有价值的贡献，但仍有若干方面有待改进。

reviews.en: The Methodologist
reviews.zh: 方法论较真派

reviews.en: My main concerns are about the statistical analysis.
reviews.zh: 我的主要疑虑在于统计分析。

reviews.en: The results are promising, but I am not yet convinced they are significant.
reviews.zh: 结果令人鼓舞，但我尚不确信其具有统计显著性。

reviews.en: How many random seeds were used? The paper does not say.
reviews.zh: 用了多少个随机种子？文中没有说明。

reviews.en: The Silent One
reviews.zh: 惜字如金型

reviews.en: Good paper.
reviews.zh: 好论文。

reviews.en: The paper is fine. Some parts could be clearer.
reviews.zh: 论文尚可。部分内容可以更清楚。

reviews.en: I have no major concerns.
reviews.zh: 无重大问题。

reviews.en: The Qualitative Purist
reviews.zh: 质性正统派

reviews.en: The study is interesting, but the qualitative method is underspecified.
reviews.zh: 研究很有意思，但质性方法交代得不够清楚。

reviews.en: I would like to know much more about the participants and the setting.
reviews.zh: 关于参与者和研究情境，我希望看到更多、更详细的介绍。

reviews.en: The paper reports what participants said, but not what the authors made of it.
reviews.zh: 本文报告了参与者说了什么，却没有说明作者从中读出了什么。

reviews.en: The Practitioner
reviews.zh: 落地派

reviews.en: As someone who builds these systems, I wonder whether this would survive a real deployment.
reviews.zh: 作为一线搭建这类系统的人，我怀疑它能否经得起真实落地的考验。

reviews.en: I like the problem. I am less sure the solution would work outside the lab.
reviews.zh: 我喜欢这个问题，但不太确定这个方案出了实验室还能不能用。

reviews.en: This could be useful in practice, if the authors address cost and latency.
reviews.zh: 如果作者能解决成本和延迟问题，这项工作在实践中可能会很有用。

reviews.en: The First-Time Reviewer
reviews.zh: 审稿萌新

reviews.en: I read this paper very carefully and have 23 comments, listed by line number.
reviews.zh: 我非常仔细地阅读了本文，共有 23 条意见，按行号列出如下。

reviews.en: Line 112 has a typo. Line 113 has another typo.
reviews.zh: 第 112 行有一处笔误。第 113 行还有一处笔误。

reviews.en: This is my first time reviewing for {venue}, so I tried to be thorough.
reviews.zh: 这是我第一次为 {venue} 审稿，所以尽量审得细致。

reviews.en: The contribution is incremental over {fake_prior}.
reviews.zh: 相较于 {fake_prior}，本文的贡献只是增量式的。

reviews.en: The proposed method is a modest extension of existing techniques.
reviews.zh: 所提方法只是对现有技术的小幅扩展。

reviews.en: The novelty over prior work on {topic} is limited.
reviews.zh: 与已有的{topic}研究相比，本文创新性不足。

reviews.en: The work is incremental given {fake_prior}, which was posted two weeks ago.
reviews.zh: 鉴于两周前刚公开的 {fake_prior}，本文只能算增量工作。

reviews.en: This has essentially been done already. See {fake_prior}, which appeared last month.
reviews.zh: 这项工作本质上已经有人做过了，见上个月发表的 {fake_prior}。

reviews.en: The approach is very similar to {fake_prior}. The paper should explain the difference.
reviews.zh: 该方法与 {fake_prior} 非常相似，文中应说明二者的区别。

reviews.en: I do not see a substantive difference between this method and {fake_prior}.
reviews.zh: 我看不出该方法与 {fake_prior} 有何实质性区别。

reviews.en: The related work misses several key papers: {fake_prior} and the six follow-up papers by the same authors.
reviews.zh: 相关工作遗漏了几篇关键论文：{fake_prior}，以及同一作者的六篇后续工作。

reviews.en: Please cite and discuss {fake_prior}, along with its six sequels, which together define this area.
reviews.zh: 请引用并讨论 {fake_prior} 及其六篇续作，它们共同定义了这一领域。

reviews.en: The main finding is already well known in the community.
reviews.zh: 主要发现在领域内早已是共识。

reviews.en: It is not surprising that current models struggle with {topic}.
reviews.zh: 现有模型在{topic}上表现不佳，这并不令人意外。

reviews.en: The results are not surprising.
reviews.zh: 结果并不出人意料。

reviews.en: The findings confirm what practitioners already suspected.
reviews.zh: 这些发现只是印证了业界早有的猜测。

reviews.en: This is a solid engineering effort, but the research contribution is unclear.
reviews.zh: 本文工程工作量饱满，但研究贡献不明确。

reviews.en: The paper describes a system, not a finding.
reviews.zh: 本文介绍的是一个系统，而非一项研究发现。

reviews.en: The method amounts to careful prompt engineering.
reviews.zh: 该方法说到底就是精心设计的提示工程。

reviews.en: Once the framing is removed, the contribution is a prompt.
reviews.zh: 去掉包装，贡献就是一条提示词。

reviews.en: With {model} now available, it is unclear whether this problem still exists.
reviews.zh: {model} 发布之后，这个问题是否依然存在，尚不清楚。

reviews.en: A stronger model would likely solve this task without the proposed method.
reviews.zh: 更强的模型很可能无需所提方法就能解决这一任务。

reviews.en: It is unclear why a new dataset is needed when existing benchmarks already cover {topic}.
