reviews.zh: 现有基准已经覆盖了{topic}，不清楚为何还需要新的数据集。

reviews.en: The paper does not explain what this benchmark measures that others do not.
reviews.zh: 文中没有说明这个基准能衡量哪些其他基准衡量不了的东西。

reviews.en: The design implications are generic; most could have been written without running the study.
reviews.zh: 设计启示过于泛泛，大部分不做这项研究也写得出来。

reviews.en: "Designers should consider users' needs" is not a design implication.
reviews.zh: “设计者应考虑用户需求”算不上设计启示。

reviews.en: The interview findings largely replicate {fake_prior}.
reviews.zh: 访谈结果在很大程度上与 {fake_prior} 重复。

reviews.en: Several of the themes are already reported in prior HCI work on {topic}.
reviews.zh: 其中若干主题，先前关于{topic}的 HCI 研究已经报道过。

reviews.en: The paper ignores decades of HCI research on this question.
reviews.zh: 本文忽视了 HCI 领域针对这一问题数十年的研究。

reviews.en: The related work cites recent NLP papers but none of the foundational HCI work on {topic}.
reviews.zh: 相关工作引用了近期的 NLP 论文，却没有引用任何关于{topic}的 HCI 奠基性工作。

reviews.en: The related work misses recent NLP work on {topic}.
reviews.zh: 相关工作遗漏了近期关于{topic}的 NLP 研究。

reviews.en: Several recent model-based approaches to this problem are not discussed.
reviews.zh: 文中未讨论近期针对该问题的几种基于模型的方法。

reviews.en: The paper reports what happens but not why.
reviews.zh: 本文报告了现象，却没有解释原因。

reviews.en: I finished the paper without a clear takeaway.
reviews.zh: 读完全文，我仍说不出本文的核心结论是什么。

reviews.en: The position is reasonable, but similar arguments have been made before.
reviews.zh: 观点合理，但类似的论点以前就有人提过。

reviews.en: I agree with the authors, which is part of the problem: so does everyone.
reviews.zh: 我同意作者的观点，而这正是问题所在：所有人都同意。

reviews.en: Current models already score above 90% on this task, so it is unclear what remains to be learned.
reviews.zh: 现有模型在该任务上已超过 90%，不清楚还有什么值得研究的。

reviews.en: The novelty of the approach could be further highlighted.
reviews.zh: 该方法的创新性可以进一步凸显。

reviews.en: It would be beneficial to further elaborate on how this work differs from existing approaches.
reviews.zh: 建议进一步阐述本工作与现有方法的区别，这将有所裨益。

reviews.en: The paper does not compare against strong recent baselines.
reviews.zh: 本文没有与近期的强 baseline 进行比较。

reviews.en: A simple retrieval baseline is missing.
reviews.zh: 缺少一个简单的检索 baseline。

reviews.en: The comparison omits the most obvious baseline: a larger model with a good prompt.
reviews.zh: 对比中漏掉了最显而易见的 baseline：更大的模型配上好的提示词。

reviews.en: The paper does not compare against {model}, which was released last week.
reviews.zh: 本文没有与上周刚发布的 {model} 进行比较。

reviews.en: Why not evaluate {model}? It came out a week ago and is clearly the new state of the art.
reviews.zh: 为什么不评测 {model}？它一周前刚发布，显然是新的 SOTA。

reviews.en: Results are reported on a single dataset, so it is unclear whether they generalize.
reviews.zh: 结果只在单一数据集上报告，泛化性存疑。

reviews.en: One dataset is not enough to support claims about {topic} in general.
reviews.zh: 一个数据集不足以支撑关于{topic}的一般性结论。

reviews.en: No significance tests are reported.
reviews.zh: 未报告显著性检验。

reviews.en: The improvements are within what I would expect from random variation.
reviews.zh: 在我看来，提升幅度仍在随机波动的范围之内。

reviews.en: Results appear to come from a single random seed.
reviews.zh: 结果似乎只来自单个随机种子。

reviews.en: Please report the mean and standard deviation over at least five seeds.
reviews.zh: 请报告至少五个随机种子下的均值和标准差。

reviews.en: The test set may have appeared in the pretraining data of the evaluated models.
reviews.zh: 测试集可能已出现在被评测模型的预训练数据中。

reviews.en: The authors do not check for data contamination.
reviews.zh: 作者没有检查数据污染。

reviews.en: Using an LLM as the judge raises concerns about bias toward its own outputs.
reviews.zh: 以 LLM 作为评判者，可能存在偏向其自身输出的问题。

reviews.en: The LLM-based evaluation is not validated against human judgments.
reviews.zh: 基于 LLM 的评测未与人工评判进行对照验证。

reviews.en: Results may be sensitive to the prompt wording, and only one prompt is reported.
reviews.zh: 结果可能对提示词措辞敏感，而文中只报告了一种提示词。

reviews.en: How were the prompts chosen? Were they tuned on the test set?
reviews.zh: 提示词是如何选定的？是否在测试集上调过？

reviews.en: The results rely on a closed API model that may change at any time, which hurts reproducibility.
reviews.zh: 结果依赖一个随时可能变动的闭源 API 模型，影响可复现性。

reviews.en: There is no ablation showing which component matters.
reviews.zh: 缺少消融实验，无法判断哪个组件真正起作用。

reviews.en: It is unclear how much each part of the method contributes.
reviews.zh: 方法各部分的贡献分别有多大，尚不清楚。

reviews.en: The ablation suggests the main component contributes very little.
reviews.zh: 消融实验表明，核心组件的贡献微乎其微。

reviews.en: Removing the proposed module barely changes the results, according to the authors' own table.
reviews.zh: 根据作者自己的表格，去掉所提模块后结果几乎不变。

reviews.en: The baselines appear under-tuned compared to the proposed method.
reviews.zh: 与所提方法相比，baseline 似乎没有充分调参。

reviews.en: The proposed method gets a hyperparameter search. The baselines get the defaults.
reviews.zh: 所提方法做了超参数搜索，baseline 用的是默认值。

reviews.en: Automatic overlap metrics may not reflect the quality humans care about.
reviews.zh: 基于重叠的自动指标未必能反映人们真正在意的质量。

reviews.en: The chosen metric rewards fluency, not correctness.
reviews.zh: 所选指标衡量的是流畅度，而非正确性。

reviews.en: The human evaluation uses only 50 examples and three annotators.
reviews.zh: 人工评测仅使用了 50 个样例和三名标注员。

reviews.en: The human evaluation is too small to support the claims.
reviews.zh: 人工评测规模太小，不足以支撑文中的结论。

reviews.en: Inter-annotator agreement is low, which calls the labels into question.
reviews.zh: 标注者间一致性偏低，标签的可靠性存疑。

reviews.en: Agreement is not reported for the human evaluation.
reviews.zh: 人工评测未报告标注一致性。

reviews.en: It is unclear whether the annotators had the expertise this task requires.
reviews.zh: 不清楚标注员是否具备该任务所需的专业知识。

reviews.en: Crowdworkers may not be qualified to judge clinical text.
reviews.zh: 众包工作者未必具备评判临床文本的专业能力。

reviews.en: Some test examples appear to be near-duplicates of training examples.
reviews.zh: 部分测试样例似乎与训练样例近乎重复。

reviews.en: The data split may leak information from train to test.
reviews.zh: 数据划分可能导致训练集信息泄漏到测试集。

reviews.en: There is no error analysis.
reviews.zh: 缺少错误分析。

reviews.en: I would like to see examples where the method fails, and why.
reviews.zh: 希望看到方法失败的例子，以及失败的原因。

reviews.en: The qualitative examples look cherry-picked.
reviews.zh: 定性示例有 cherry-pick 之嫌。

reviews.en: The examples in the case study seem chosen to flatter the method.
reviews.zh: 案例分析中的例子似乎是专门挑来给方法脸上贴金的。

reviews.en: The paper does not report the computational cost.
reviews.zh: 本文未报告计算开销。

reviews.en: Is the improvement worth five times the inference cost?
reviews.zh: 为这点提升付出五倍推理开销，值得吗？

reviews.en: All experiments are in English, which the paper should state explicitly.
reviews.zh: 所有实验均基于英文，文中应明确说明。

reviews.en: Would the findings hold for languages other than English?
reviews.zh: 这些发现在英语以外的语言上是否依然成立？

reviews.en: It is unclear whether this would work in a real deployment, with real latency and real users.
reviews.zh: 放到真实部署中，面对真实的延迟和真实的用户，该方法是否奏效尚不清楚。

reviews.en: The setting assumes clean inputs that real systems never see.
reviews.zh: 实验设定假设输入都很干净，而真实系统从来碰不到这么干净的输入。

reviews.en: My main concern is that the paper never explains how the evaluation data was collected.
reviews.zh: 我的主要疑虑是，文中从未说明评测数据是如何收集的。

reviews.en: It is unclear which model is used as the backbone.
reviews.zh: 不清楚 backbone 用的是哪个模型。

reviews.en: The paper does not say how participants were recruited.
reviews.zh: 文中没有说明参与者是如何招募的。

reviews.en: The experimental evaluation could be more comprehensive.
reviews.zh: 实验评估可以更加全面。

reviews.en: Additional experiments would further strengthen the paper's claims.
reviews.zh: 补充更多实验将进一步增强本文结论的说服力。

reviews.en: With 12 participants, the findings may not generalize.
reviews.zh: 仅有 12 名参与者，研究发现未必具有普适性。

reviews.en: The sample size is small for the strength of the claims.
reviews.zh: 相对于结论的力度，样本量偏小。

reviews.en: The study should be repeated with a much larger sample of clinicians, ideally at several hospitals.
reviews.zh: 建议在规模大得多的临床医生样本上重复这项研究，最好覆盖多家医院。

reviews.en: I would like to see a large-scale deployment before drawing these conclusions.
reviews.zh: 要得出这些结论，我希望先看到大规模部署的结果。

reviews.en: Twelve clinicians is a pilot, not a study. Please recruit more.
reviews.zh: 十二位临床医生只能算预实验，不能算研究。请招募更多参与者。

reviews.en: Participants were recruited from the authors' own institution, which may bias the results.
reviews.zh: 参与者来自作者所在机构，可能使结果产生偏差。

reviews.en: Most participants appear to be students, not the intended users.
reviews.zh: 大多数参与者似乎是学生，而非目标用户。

reviews.en: No power analysis justifies the sample size.
reviews.zh: 样本量缺乏功效分析（power analysis）支撑。

reviews.en: A lab study cannot show how the tool would be used in a real clinic.
reviews.zh: 实验室研究无法说明医生在真实门诊中会怎样使用这个工具。

reviews.en: The tasks are performed outside the participants' real workflow.
reviews.zh: 实验任务脱离了参与者的真实工作流程。

reviews.en: The positive ratings may reflect a novelty effect.
reviews.zh: 正面评分可能源于新奇效应。

reviews.en: A one-session study cannot tell us whether people would keep using the tool.
reviews.zh: 仅凭一次实验，无法判断用户是否会持续使用该工具。

reviews.en: Likert responses are analyzed with t-tests; non-parametric tests would be more appropriate.
reviews.zh: 李克特量表数据用 t 检验分析，换用非参数检验会更合适。

reviews.en: Averaging Likert items as if they were interval data needs justification.
reviews.zh: 把李克特题目当作等距数据取平均，需要给出理由。

reviews.en: The qualitative analysis is underspecified. Who coded the data, and how were disagreements resolved?
reviews.zh: 质性分析交代不清。数据由谁编码？分歧又是如何解决的？

reviews.en: "Themes emerged from the data" is not a description of a method.
reviews.zh: “主题从数据中浮现”算不上方法描述。

reviews.en: No inter-rater reliability is reported for the qualitative coding.
reviews.zh: 质性编码未报告评分者间信度。

reviews.en: Participants knew the authors built the system, which may have inflated their ratings.
reviews.zh: 参与者知道系统是作者开发的，这可能抬高了评分。

reviews.en: The experimenter was in the room during sessions, which may have influenced the responses.
reviews.zh: 实验过程中实验者一直在场，可能影响了参与者的回答。

reviews.en: The task scenarios do not reflect real clinical workflows.
reviews.zh: 任务场景不能反映真实的临床工作流程。

reviews.en: No clinician would encounter this scenario in practice.
reviews.zh: 实际工作中没有哪位临床医生会遇到这种场景。

reviews.en: The study has no baseline condition, so it is unclear what the tool is better than.
reviews.zh: 研究没有设置基线条件，因此不清楚这个工具究竟比什么更好。

reviews.en: Without a control condition, the positive results are hard to interpret.
reviews.zh: 没有对照条件，正面结果难以解读。

reviews.en: All measures are self-reported; actual behavior was not measured.
reviews.zh: 所有指标均为自我报告，未测量实际行为。

reviews.en: Perceived usefulness is not the same as usefulness.
reviews.zh: 感知有用性不等于实际有用性。

reviews.en: The order of conditions was not counterbalanced.
reviews.zh: 未对条件顺序进行平衡处理。

reviews.en: The online survey has no attention checks, so some responses may come from bots.
reviews.zh: 线上问卷没有注意力检查题，部分回答可能来自机器人。

reviews.en: The pilot participants appear to be lab members, who may not represent the target users.
reviews.zh: 预实验参与者似乎是实验室成员，未必能代表目标用户。

reviews.en: The paper is hard to follow.
reviews.zh: 本文读起来很吃力。

reviews.en: I had to read Section 3 three times to understand the method.
reviews.zh: 我把第 3 节读了三遍才看懂方法。

reviews.en: The motivation is unclear. Why does this problem matter, and to whom?
reviews.zh: 动机不清楚。这个问题为什么重要？对谁重要？

reviews.en: It is not clear who would use this, or why.
reviews.zh: 不清楚谁会用它，又为什么要用。

reviews.en: The notation changes between Sections 3 and 4.
reviews.zh: 第 3 节和第 4 节的符号不一致。

reviews.en: The same quantity has three different names in the paper.
reviews.zh: 同一个量在文中有三个不同的名字。

reviews.en: Figure 2 is unreadable when printed.
reviews.zh: 图 2 打印出来根本看不清。

reviews.en: The axis labels in Figure 3 are too small to read.
reviews.zh: 图 3 的坐标轴标签太小，无法辨认。

reviews.en: The abstract claims more than the results show.
reviews.zh: 摘要的说法超出了结果所能支持的范围。

reviews.en: "Solves" is a strong word for a two-point gain.
reviews.zh: 提升两个点就说“解决”，用词过重。

reviews.en: Too much is pushed to the appendix, so the main paper is not self-contained.
reviews.zh: 太多内容放进了附录，只读正文看不明白。

reviews.en: The paper has many typos and needs proofreading.
reviews.zh: 文中笔误较多，建议仔细校对。

reviews.en: Line 112 contains a typo. So do lines 140, 141 and 207.
reviews.zh: 第 112 行有笔误。第 140、141 和 207 行也有。

reviews.en: Important implementation details are missing, so the work cannot be reproduced.
reviews.zh: 缺少重要的实现细节，工作无法复现。

reviews.en: The paper does not give enough detail to replicate the study.
reviews.zh: 文中给出的细节不足以复现这项研究。

reviews.en: The paper uses NLP terms without explanation, which will lose HCI readers.
reviews.zh: 文中使用 NLP 术语却不加解释，HCI 读者会看不懂。

reviews.en: The paper assumes familiarity with HCI methods that many readers at {venue} will not have.
reviews.zh: 本文默认读者熟悉 HCI 方法，而 {venue} 的很多读者并不熟悉。

reviews.en: The contributions are not clearly stated.
reviews.zh: 本文的贡献点阐述不清。

reviews.en: After the introduction, I was still not sure what the paper contributes.
reviews.zh: 读完引言，我仍不确定本文的贡献是什么。

reviews.en: The paper tries to make four contributions and makes none of them clearly.
reviews.zh: 本文试图做出四项贡献，却没有一项讲清楚。

reviews.en: A dataset, a method, a user study and a benchmark is too much for one paper.
reviews.zh: 一个数据集、一个方法、一项用户研究加一个基准，对一篇论文来说太多了。

reviews.en: The study design is spread across four sections and is hard to reconstruct.
reviews.zh: 研究设计散落在四个章节中，很难拼出全貌。

reviews.en: I could not tell how many sessions each participant completed, or in what order.
reviews.zh: 我看不出每位参与者完成了几次实验，顺序又是怎样的。

reviews.en: The title promises more than the paper delivers.
reviews.zh: 标题许诺的，比论文实际做到的多。

reviews.en: The Limitations section is a single generic sentence.
reviews.zh: Limitations 一节只有一句泛泛而谈的话。

reviews.en: The main result appears only on page 7.
reviews.zh: 主要结果直到第 7 页才出现。

reviews.en: The key finding is hidden in the middle of Section 5.
reviews.zh: 关键发现藏在第 5 节中间。

reviews.en: Table 2 has 14 columns and no clear takeaway.
reviews.zh: 表 2 有 14 列，却看不出明确的结论。

reviews.en: Participant roles and experience are not reported.
reviews.zh: 未报告参与者的岗位和从业经验。

reviews.en: The participant table should describe the participants in much more detail.
reviews.zh: 参与者信息表过于简略，应补充更多细节。

reviews.en: The findings section is mostly quotes, with little analysis connecting them.
reviews.zh: 研究发现部分大多是引语，缺少将它们串联起来的分析。

reviews.en: Several paragraphs end with a single word on their last line.
reviews.zh: 有好几段的最后一行只剩一个单词。

reviews.en: The paper could benefit from further clarification of certain aspects.
reviews.zh: 本文的某些方面若能进一步阐明，将会更加完善。

reviews.en: Some sections could be more concise and clearer.
reviews.zh: 部分章节可以更加简洁、清晰。

reviews.en: The authors should discuss the limitations of their approach in more detail.
reviews.zh: 作者应更详细地讨论其方法的局限性。

reviews.en: A dedicated limitations section would strengthen the paper.
reviews.zh: 增设专门的局限性章节将进一步提升本文质量。

reviews.en: This is an HCI paper. I am not sure what the NLP contribution is.
reviews.zh: 这是一篇 HCI 论文。我不确定它在 NLP 上的贡献是什么。

reviews.en: There is no new model or method, so it is unclear why this paper is at {venue}.
reviews.zh: 没有新模型，也没有新方法，不清楚这篇论文为什么投 {venue}。

reviews.en: The paper is mainly a modeling contribution; the user study feels added on.
reviews.zh: 本文主要是建模方面的贡献，用户研究像是后来加上去的。

reviews.en: The human-centered part is too thin for {venue}.
reviews.zh: 对 {venue} 来说，以人为本的部分太单薄了。

reviews.en: This would make a good workshop paper.
reviews.zh: 这会是一篇不错的 workshop 论文。

reviews.en: The contribution is better suited to a workshop.
reviews.zh: 这一贡献更适合 workshop。

reviews.en: The natural audience for this work is clinical informatics, not {venue}.
reviews.zh: 这项工作的天然受众在临床信息学领域，而不是 {venue}。

reviews.en: This might be better received at a medical informatics venue.
reviews.zh: 投医学信息学方向的会议或期刊，可能会更受欢迎。

reviews.en: The paper may fit better in a different track.
reviews.zh: 本文或许更适合其他 track。

reviews.en: The work is too applied for {venue}.
reviews.zh: 对 {venue} 来说，这项工作太偏应用了。

reviews.en: This is a nice application, but where is the general lesson?
reviews.zh: 这是个不错的应用，但普适的启示在哪里？

reviews.en: The paper studies a narrow setting of limited interest to the broader community.
reviews.zh: 本文研究的场景过于狭窄，对更广泛的学术社区吸引力有限。

reviews.en: Results from one hospital in one specialty may not interest most of the {venue} audience.
reviews.zh: 一家医院、一个专科的结果，{venue} 的大多数读者恐怕不会感兴趣。

reviews.en: The paper lacks the learning contribution expected at {venue}.
reviews.zh: 本文缺少 {venue} 所期待的机器学习贡献。

reviews.en: The ethics statement does not discuss risks to patients.
reviews.zh: 伦理声明没有讨论对患者的风险。

reviews.en: The paper should discuss how the system could cause harm when it is wrong.
reviews.zh: 本文应讨论系统出错时可能造成哪些伤害。

reviews.en: The responsible research checklist says the code will be released, but the paper does not say where.
reviews.zh: 负责任研究清单上写着会公开代码，但文中没说在哪里公开。

reviews.en: The paper was submitted to the special theme but does not engage with it.
reviews.zh: 本文投的是特别主题，却没有真正回应这个主题。

reviews.en: The broader impact of this work could be discussed more thoroughly.
reviews.zh: 可以更充分地讨论这项工作的更广泛影响。

reviews.en: The authors may wish to consider the broader implications of their work for society.
reviews.zh: 作者不妨考虑一下其工作对社会的更广泛意义。

reviews.en: The reviewers agree that the paper makes a clear contribution, and the rebuttal resolved the main concerns. Accept.
reviews.zh: 审稿人一致认为本文贡献明确，rebuttal 也解决了主要疑虑。接收。

reviews.en: All reviewers see value in this work. Please make the promised changes in the final version.
reviews.zh: 所有审稿人都认可这项工作的价值。请在终稿中完成承诺的修改。

reviews.en: Despite some concerns about scope, this is a solid contribution to {venue}. Accept.
reviews.zh: 尽管研究范围方面存在一些疑虑，本文仍是一篇适合 {venue} 的扎实工作。接收。

reviews.en: The author response convinced two reviewers, and I agree with them. Accept.
reviews.zh: 作者回复说服了两位审稿人，我也同意他们的看法。接收。

reviews.en: A timely study of {topic} with a careful evaluation. Accept, with minor revisions to the presentation.
reviews.zh: 一项关于{topic}的及时研究，评估严谨。接收，表述上需小修。

reviews.en: Reviewer 2 raises valid points, but they can be addressed in the camera-ready. Accept.
reviews.zh: 2 号审稿人提出的问题有道理，但可以在终稿中解决。接收。

reviews.en: A clear, well-executed paper. I recommend acceptance and encourage the authors to release their code.
reviews.zh: 论文清晰，完成度高。建议接收，并鼓励作者公开代码。

reviews.en: The paper is sound, but the contribution is modest for the main conference. Recommended for Findings.
reviews.zh: 论文扎实，但就主会而言贡献偏小。推荐收录至 Findings。

reviews.en: Reviewers appreciate the careful experiments but question the novelty. Findings is a good home for this work.
reviews.zh: 审稿人肯定了细致的实验，但质疑其新颖性。Findings 是这项工作不错的归宿。

reviews.en: Solid but incremental. Findings.
reviews.zh: 扎实但偏增量。Findings。

reviews.en: The rebuttal addressed several concerns, though not enough for the main conference. Findings.
reviews.zh: rebuttal 解决了若干疑虑，但还不足以进入主会。Findings。

reviews.en: A useful resource for the community; the analysis could go deeper. Findings.
reviews.zh: 对社区而言是有用的资源，但分析可以更深入。Findings。

reviews.en: The reviewers are split, but the work is sound. Findings is the right venue for it.
reviews.zh: 审稿人意见不一，但工作本身扎实。Findings 是它合适的去处。

reviews.en: The reviewers raise concerns about soundness that the rebuttal did not fully resolve. Reject.
reviews.zh: 审稿人对方法的可靠性提出了疑虑，rebuttal 未能完全解决。拒稿。

reviews.en: While the topic is important, the contribution is not yet clear. We encourage the authors to resubmit.
reviews.zh: 选题很重要，但贡献尚不明确。鼓励作者修改后重投。

reviews.en: Two reviewers find the evaluation insufficient, and I agree. Reject.
reviews.zh: 两位审稿人认为评估不充分，我同意。拒稿。

reviews.en: The paper has potential, but the current version is not ready for {venue}.
reviews.zh: 论文有潜力，但当前版本还达不到 {venue} 的要求。

reviews.en: Reviewers question whether {venue} is the right venue for this work. Reject.
reviews.zh: 审稿人质疑本文是否适合投 {venue}。拒稿。

reviews.en: The rebuttal was appreciated but did not change the reviewers' assessment. Reject.
reviews.zh: 感谢作者的 rebuttal，但审稿人的评价没有改变。拒稿。

reviews.en: Reviewer 3's concerns are serious and were not resolved. Reject.
reviews.zh: 3 号审稿人的疑虑很严重，且未得到解决。拒稿。

reviews.en: The reviewers see value in this work but request substantial revisions. Revise and resubmit.
reviews.zh: 审稿人认可这项工作的价值，但要求大幅修改。大修重投。

reviews.en: The study is promising, but the analysis needs to be rewritten. Revise and resubmit.
reviews.zh: 研究很有前景，但分析部分需要重写。大修重投。

reviews.en: Please address every reviewer concern, especially the framing of the contribution, and resubmit.
reviews.zh: 请逐条回应审稿意见，尤其是贡献的定位，然后重投。

reviews.en: The committee asks for a revised version with a clearer account of the study design and the participants.
reviews.zh: 程序委员会要求提交修改稿，更清楚地说明研究设计和参与者情况。

reviews.en: Major revision: the reviewers ask for a deeper discussion of the design implications.
reviews.zh: 大修：审稿人要求更深入地讨论设计启示。

reviews.en: The paper is close. A careful revision that addresses R1 and R3 could make it a strong contribution.
reviews.zh: 论文离接收只差一步。若能认真修改、回应 R1 和 R3 的意见，有望成为一篇有分量的工作。

side.en: Hit the gym three times
side.zh: 去健身房打卡三次

side.en: Your body will thank you, eventually.
side.zh: 身体总有一天会感谢你的。

side.en: Sore on Tuesday, smug on Thursday.
side.zh: 周二浑身酸痛，周四开始发朋友圈。

side.en: Join {labmate}'s Saturday run club
side.zh: 加入 {labmate} 的周六跑团

side.en: Five kilometers, then pastries.
side.zh: 先跑五公里，再吃点心。

side.en: You finish last and nobody minds. The pastries are excellent.
side.zh: 你跑了个倒数第一，也没人在意。点心是真的好吃。

side.en: Try the free yoga class at the rec center
side.zh: 去体育馆试试免费瑜伽课

side.en: Your shoulders have been up by your ears since September.
side.zh: 从九月开始，你的肩膀就一直耸到耳朵边。

side.en: You can't touch your toes. You can, however, unclench your jaw.
side.zh: 你还是摸不到脚尖，不过咬紧的牙关总算松开了。

side.en: Finally see a doctor about that cough
side.zh: 终于去医院看咳嗽

side.en: It's been three weeks, and your labmates have noticed.
side.zh: 已经咳了三周，连同门都注意到了。

side.en: The doctor prescribes rest and says "you should sleep more" like it's easy.
side.zh: 医生让你好好休息，轻飘飘来了句“要多睡觉”，说得跟很容易似的。

side.en: Cook real food on Sunday
side.zh: 周日正经做顿饭

side.en: Five lunches that aren't vending machine crackers.
side.zh: 五顿不靠外卖的午饭。

side.en: You make five containers of lentil soup. By Thursday you never want to see a lentil again.
side.zh: 你做了五盒咖喱鸡。到周四，你这辈子都不想再看见咖喱了。

side.en: Go to bed before midnight, every night
side.zh: 每晚十二点前上床

side.en: A radical experiment.
side.zh: 一项激进的实验。

side.en: It works. You're annoyed by how well it works.
side.zh: 居然真管用，管用到让你有点不爽。

side.en: Take Friday afternoon off
side.zh: 周五下午翘个班

side.en: The paper will still be there on Monday.
side.zh: 论文周一还在那儿，跑不了。

side.en: You take a long walk, then a longer nap.
side.zh: 你散了很久的步，又睡了更久的午觉。

side.en: Board game night at {labmate}'s place
side.zh: 去 {labmate} 家玩桌游

side.en: Someone always brings a game with forty pages of rules.
side.zh: 总有人带来一款规则书四十页厚的游戏。

side.en: Nobody understands the rules by the end. Everyone has a great time.
side.zh: 到最后也没人搞懂规则，但大家都玩得很开心。

side.en: Dinner with friends from outside the lab
side.zh: 约组外的朋友吃饭

side.en: People who don't know what a p-value is.
side.zh: 一群不知道 p 值是什么的人。

side.en: Nobody asks about your paper. It's the best two hours of the month.
side.zh: 没人问你论文的事，这是这个月最快乐的两个小时。

side.en: Call home for an hour
side.zh: 给家里打一小时电话

side.en: They miss you.
side.zh: 家里人想你了。

side.en: You hear all about the neighbor's dog and your cousin's wedding, and for an hour you forget about the lab.
side.zh: 你听完了邻居家狗狗的近况和亲戚家的婚礼八卦，整整一个小时没想起实验室。

side.en: Go on a day hike
side.zh: 去徒步一天

side.en: You haven't seen a tree up close since August.
side.zh: 你从八月起就没近距离看过一棵树了。

side.en: You spend six hours outside with no signal and one very good sandwich.
side.zh: 你在户外待了六个小时，没有信号，只有一个超好吃的三明治。

side.en: The trails are open again.
side.zh: 步道又开放了。

side.en: See a concert downtown
side.zh: 去市中心听演唱会

side.en: Loud music, no slides.
side.zh: 音乐够响，没有 PPT。

side.en: Your ears ring all Sunday, and you don't think about your paper once.
side.zh: 耳朵嗡嗡响了一整个周日，但你一次都没想起论文。

side.en: Two evenings with your old hobby
side.zh: 花两个晚上重拾旧爱好

side.en: The one you had before you had a research agenda.
side.zh: 就是你有“研究方向”之前的那个。

side.en: You're rusty, and it doesn't matter at all.
side.zh: 手生了，不过一点也不要紧。

side.en: Get coffee with the visiting speaker
side.zh: 和来访讲者喝杯咖啡

side.en: You had a question, and the Q&A ran out of time.
side.zh: 你本来有个问题，可问答环节没时间了。

side.en: Over coffee, they ask a sharp question about {project} you hadn't thought of.
side.zh: 喝咖啡时，对方就 {project} 问了个犀利的问题，你之前完全没想到。

side.en: Go to the department reading group
side.zh: 去系里的读书会

side.en: Free pizza and someone else's paper.
side.zh: 免费披萨，外加别人的论文。

side.en: The discussion is better than the paper, and it gives you an idea for {project}.
side.zh: 讨论比论文本身精彩，还让你对 {project} 有了个新想法。

side.en: Help {labmate} debug their training run
side.zh: 帮 {labmate} 调训练的 bug

side.en: "It's probably a quick fix."
side.zh: “应该很快就能修好。”

side.en: It's a learning rate. It's always a learning rate. They owe you one.
side.zh: 是学习率。永远都是学习率。对方欠你一个人情。

side.en: Show a visiting friend around town
side.zh: 陪来玩的朋友逛逛

side.en: An old friend from undergrad is in town for the weekend.
side.zh: 本科时的一个老朋友周末来你这儿玩。

side.en: You show them around and find out you know more good restaurants than you thought.
side.zh: 你带朋友四处转了转，发现自己私藏的好馆子比想象中多。

side.en: Host your parents for a weekend
side.zh: 接爸妈来住一个周末

side.en: They want to see "where you work".
side.zh: 爸妈想看看“你上班的地方”。

side.en: They take a photo of you next to your desk and send it to the whole family.
side.zh: 爸妈给你和工位拍了张合影，发到了家族群里。

side.en: Sign up for the department step challenge
side.zh: 报名系里的步数挑战赛

side.en: The staff team has won three years running.
side.zh: 行政老师队已经三连冠了。

side.en: You take the stairs every day and still lose to the staff team, but your legs feel great.
side.zh: 你天天爬楼梯，还是输给了行政老师队。不过腿脚倒是利索多了。

side.en: Drop in on a workshop in the next city
side.zh: 去邻市蹭个 workshop

side.en: Free student registration, one train ride away.
side.zh: 学生免费注册，坐趟高铁就到。

side.en: The conversations run long, and you come home with new ideas for {project}.
side.zh: 大家聊得停不下来，你带着关于 {project} 的新想法回了家。

side.en: Bike to campus instead of taking the bus
side.zh: 改骑车去学校，不坐公交

side.en: The weather is good, and the bus is always late anyway.
side.zh: 天气不错，反正公交也总晚点。

side.en: Twenty minutes each way. You arrive awake for once.
side.zh: 单程二十分钟，你难得清醒着到了学校。

side.en: Go to the dentist appointment you've moved three times
side.zh: 去看改了三次期的牙医

side.en: They've stopped sending reminders and started sending worried emails.
side.zh: 诊所已经不发提醒，改发担心你的邮件了。

side.en: You get one small filling and a lecture about grinding your teeth when stressed.
side.zh: 你补了个小牙洞，还听医生念叨了半天压力大会磨牙。

statuses.en: Free days halved and no overtime for a few weeks.
statuses.zh: 接下来几周可用天数减半，不能加班。

statuses.en: Stress rises each week; working at 90%.
statuses.zh: 压力每周上升；工作效率 90%。

statuses.en: Working at 115%, but it adds Stress.
statuses.zh: 工作效率 115%，但压力会增加。

statuses.en: The routine is paused for the internship.
statuses.zh: 实习期间，日常安排暂停。

statuses.en: No research; Stress eases and Health recovers.
statuses.zh: 不做研究；压力缓解，健康恢复。

statuses.en: Part of every week goes to the thesis and slides.
statuses.zh: 每周要分出一部分时间写博士论文、做幻灯片。

statuses.en: Quals are coming. "Prepare for quals" raises your odds.
statuses.zh: 资格考试快到了。选“准备资格考试”能提高通过率。

statuses.en: Project days count toward proposal readiness.
statuses.zh: 花在项目上的天数会计入开题准备度。

tips.en: Classes have answers in the back of the book. Research doesn't, so the sooner you stop looking for them, the better.
tips.zh: 上课做题，书后面有答案。研究可没有，越早放下找答案的念头越好。

tips.en: Ask yourself why you're here, and be more honest than your statement of purpose was.
tips.zh: 问问自己为什么来读博，答案要比你 PS 里写的诚实一点。

tips.en: A harsh review is a free lesson from someone who read your paper closely. It just doesn't feel free.
tips.zh: 尖刻的审稿意见，其实是认真读过你论文的人免费给你上的一课。只是上完挺肉疼的。

tips.en: If citations are the only thing keeping you going, you'll run dry. Find what you'd do even if nobody cited it.
tips.zh: 要是只靠引用数撑着，迟早会被掏空。找一件就算没人引用，你也愿意做的事。

tips.en: The degree is just the receipt for what you actually bought: the training.
tips.zh: 学位只是张小票。你真正买到的，是这几年的训练。

tips.en: Don't aim for borderline. Borderline is a coin flip with extra steps.
tips.zh: 别把目标定在踩线。踩线中不中，跟抛硬币差不多，只是流程更长。

tips.en: Whatever you promised in that rebuttal, do it. People remember who delivers.
tips.zh: rebuttal 里答应过的，都要做到。谁靠谱，大家心里有数。

tips.en: Stop counting other people's papers. You aren't running the same race.
tips.zh: 别老数别人发了几篇。你们跑的根本不是同一场比赛。

tips.en: When you get stuck, learn the method behind the fix. You'll be stuck again.
tips.zh: 卡住的时候，别只记住怎么解，要弄懂背后的方法。你还会再卡住的。

tips.en: Everyone starts strong. The middle years are the hard part, so pace yourself to finish.
tips.zh: 谁刚开始都劲头十足。难熬的是中间那几年，悠着点，才跑得到终点。

tips.en: At some point it stops being your advisor's agenda. Make sure it becomes yours.
tips.zh: 读到某个阶段，课题就不该只是老板的了。得让它真正变成你自己的。

tips.en: Snowball from one great paper: what it cites, and what cites it. Two hours of that beats a week of keyword searching.
tips.zh: 从一篇好论文开始滚雪球：看它引了谁，再看谁引了它。这样花两小时，比搜一周关键词管用。

tips.en: Not every paper deserves a full read. Learn which ones do.
tips.zh: 不是每篇论文都值得从头读到尾，要学会分辨哪些值得。

tips.en: To learn a method, pick a paper you admire and work out how they did it.
tips.zh: 想学一个方法，就找篇你服气的论文，琢磨人家是怎么做出来的。

tips.en: Walk into advisor meetings with answers, and walk out with better ones.
tips.zh: 去见老板，要带着答案进去，带着更好的答案出来。

tips.en: If you can delete a paragraph and nothing breaks, delete it.
tips.zh: 一段话删了什么都不影响，那就删。

tips.en: Write for a tired reviewer who is reading your paper fourth today.
tips.zh: 写的时候想象一个累坏了的审稿人，你这篇是对方今天看的第四篇。

tips.en: Before you start a project, try answering ten hard questions about it. The ones you can't answer show you where to start.
tips.zh: 开项目之前，先试着回答关于它的十个难题。答不上来的那几个，就是你该下手的地方。

tips.en: If you can't state your research question in one sentence, you don't have one yet.
tips.zh: 一句话说不清研究问题，说明你还没有研究问题。

tips.en: Who cares, and what has already been done? Answer those two and the introduction writes itself.
tips.zh: 谁在乎？别人做过什么？这两个答好了，引言就写得差不多了。

tips.en: Your method should follow from the gap. If it doesn't, one of them is wrong.
tips.zh: 方法应该从研究空白里顺出来。顺不出来，说明两者里总有一个错了。

tips.en: Watch what people actually do between the clicks. That's where the design problems are.
tips.zh: 去看用户两次点击之间到底在干嘛。设计问题都藏在那儿。

tips.en: A result is a number. A finding says what the number means, and that's what reviewers want.
tips.zh: 结果只是个数字，发现要说清这个数字意味着什么。审稿人要的是后者。

tips.en: Pick the venue whose readers will care most, not the one with the nicest logo.
tips.zh: 投稿要挑读者最在乎这项工作的会，别挑 logo 最好看的。

tips.en: Burnout builds up slowly, one skipped weekend at a time.
tips.zh: 倦怠是一点点攒出来的，每少休一个周末，就多攒一点。

tips.en: Your limits change every year of the PhD, so check them again.
tips.zh: 读博的每一年，你的极限都在变，记得时不时重新摸摸底。

tips.en: Closing the laptop doesn't count as rest if you're still thinking about work.
tips.zh: 电脑合上了，脑子还在想工作，那不叫休息。

tips.en: You only have a few real hours of deep focus a day. Spend them on the hard part.
tips.zh: 一天里真能专注的就那么几个小时，要留给最难的那部分。

titles.zh: 论文过了同行评审，奶茶过了珍珠评审。

titles.en: A thousand citations. People cite you without reading you now.
titles.zh: 引用破千。现在大家引你的论文，连读都不用读了。

titles.en: An h-index most postdocs would envy.
titles.zh: h 指数高到大多数博士后都眼红。

titles.en: Plenty of citations, and more than one burnout along the way.
titles.zh: 引用不少，一路上也倦怠了不止一次。

titles.en: Burned out three times and came back every time.
titles.zh: 倦怠了三次，每次都爬了回来。

titles.en: Rejected again and again, and published anyway.
titles.zh: 屡投屡拒，屡拒屡投，最后还是发了。

titles.en: Done in four years or less.
Seven years or more, by the scenic route.
titles.zh: 七年或更久，一路看风景。

titles.en: Graduated without burning out or living in the lab.
titles.zh: 顺利毕业，没倦怠，也没住进实验室。

titles.en: A hundred and twenty weekend days in the lab.
titles.zh: 周末在实验室泡了 120 天。

titles.en: Everyone knows you, even people you've never met.
titles.zh: 人人都认识你，连没见过面的人也认识你。

titles.en: You raised the lab's junior students.
titles.zh: 组里的师弟师妹都是你带大的。

titles.en: Three workshop papers, and good conversations in small rooms.
titles.zh: 三篇 workshop 论文，外加小会议室里那些聊得投机的讨论。

titles.en: You read everything, including the appendices.
titles.zh: 你什么都读，连附录也不放过。

titles.en: The lab's events don't happen without you.
titles.zh: 没有你，组里的活动就办不起来。

titles.en: You skipped two deadlines to do it right.
titles.zh: 为了把事做对，你放掉了两次截稿。

titles.en: You and your laptop against the world.
titles.zh: 你和一台笔记本，单挑全世界。

titles.en: You found out what you don't want, which is a useful start.
titles.zh: 你搞清楚了自己不想要什么，这是个不错的开始。

titles.en: Solid work with no drama, and a degree you earned.
titles.zh: 活儿扎实，没什么狗血剧情，学位是你自己挣来的。

教育中的 AI 反馈
专业工作流中的 LLM 智能体
自然语言处理中的隐私问题

traits.zh: 早上开会额外增加压力。
截稿前熬夜会额外消耗精力。

traits.en: Every stage takes longer; rejections sting more.
traits.zh: 每个阶段都更耗时；被拒时更受打击。

traits.en: Huge bursts in the last weeks before a deadline.
traits.zh: 截稿前最后几周爆发力惊人。

traits.en: Slow at the start of every stage.
traits.zh: 每个阶段刚开始时进展缓慢。

traits.en: Prepares hard: bonus in quals, proposal and defense.
traits.zh: 准备格外充分：资格考试、开题和答辩都有加成。

traits.en: Network grows 50% faster; social days restore more.
traits.zh: 人脉增长快 50%；见朋友的日子恢复得更多。
读论文和写作的速度快 10%。
拓展人脉会额外消耗精力。
其实没有。技多不压身嘛。

traits.en: Grumpy after six weeks without exercise.
An extra effective day when Energy runs low.
traits.zh: 精力不足时，多出一天有效工作日。
收到更多邀请和合作署名。
每答应一次，就搭进去一天。

traits.en: Rare and legendary events come more often.
traits.zh: 稀有和传说事件出现得更频繁。

traits.en: Other people will think you're good.
traits.zh: 别人会以为你全靠实力。

traits.en: Even good news adds a little Stress.
traits.zh: 连好消息都会让压力涨一点。
拓展人脉带来的引用多 30%。
居家生活能缓解更多压力。

traits.en: Nobody told you the unwritten rules.
traits.zh: 没人告诉过你那些不成文的规矩。

traits.en: Works 10% faster; a strong buffer against Stress.
traits.zh: 工作速度快 10%；能大幅缓冲压力。

traits.en: One fixed family day every week.

traits.zh: 花在爱好上的日子，多缓解 50% 压力。
偶尔有演出会占掉一天。
分析阶段的成果更扎实。

traits.en: Methods reviewers love you a bit too much.
traits.zh: 搞方法的审稿人对你格外“关照”。

traits.en: Stress eases a little every week.
traits.zh: 压力每周都会缓解一点。

traits.en: Deadlines are always closer than they appear.
traits.zh: 截稿日期永远比看起来更近。

traits.en: Extra network at conferences; two sets of holidays.
traits.zh: 参会时人脉额外加成；能过两套节日。

traits.en: Visas, time zones, and family far away.
traits.zh: 签证、时差，还有远方的家人。

traits.en: Coding and network start much higher.
traits.zh: 编程和人脉初始值高很多。

traits.en: Domain knowledge starts high; user studies go better.
traits.zh: 领域知识初始值高；用户研究更顺利。

traits.en: You arrive with a half-finished project.
traits.zh: 入学时就带着一个做了一半的项目。

traits.en: It comes with someone else's old decisions.
traits.zh: 附赠一堆别人当年拍板的祖传决定。

traits.en: You know your limits now: Stress eases faster.
traits.zh: 你现在知道自己的极限了：压力缓解得更快。
截稿冲刺会带来更多压力。

advisor.en: Quick Question
advisor.zh: 有个小问题

advisor.en: At 11:04 pm, {advisor} sends an email with the subject line "quick question". The question is not quick.
advisor.zh: 晚上 11:04，{advisor}发来一封邮件，标题是“有个小问题”。问题一点也不小。

advisor.en: Your phone buzzes at 11 pm: "Quick question: could you rerun everything with the new data split?"
advisor.zh: 晚上 11 点，你的手机震了：“有个小问题：能不能用新的数据划分把所有实验重跑一遍？”

advisor.en: Answer it tonight
advisor.zh: 今晚就回

advisor.en: You reply at 12:40 am, and {advisor} answers "thx" at 12:41, which from them is high praise.
advisor.zh: 你凌晨 12:40 回了信，{advisor}在 12:41 回了句“感谢”。在老板那里，这已经算是夸你了。

advisor.en: Reply in the morning
advisor.zh: 明早再回

advisor.en: You sleep. By morning, a second email from {advisor} has answered the first one.
advisor.zh: 你去睡了。到了早上，{advisor}的第二封邮件说，第一封里的问题已经解决了。

advisor.en: Send "On it tomorrow!"
advisor.zh: 回一句“收到，明天弄！”

advisor.en: A thumbs-up comes back, and everyone gets to sleep.
advisor.zh: 对面回了个大拇指，大家都能去睡了。

advisor.en: Two more "quick" emails arrive before midnight. You read them all.
advisor.zh: 午夜前又来了两封“有个小问题”。你每封都读了。

advisor.en: Due Friday
advisor.zh: 周五截止

advisor.en: {advisor} needs help with a grant proposal due Friday. "Just the preliminary results section. You know the work best."
advisor.zh: {advisor}的基金申请周五截止，找你帮忙。“就写初步结果那一节，这块你最熟。”

advisor.en: Write the section
advisor.zh: 写这一节

advisor.en: You write four pages about your own work in the future tense. {advisor} is clearly grateful.
advisor.zh: 你把自己做完的工作写成了四页“我们将会……”。{advisor}显然很感激。

advisor.en: Offer figures, not prose
advisor.zh: 只给图，不写字

advisor.en: You send two clean figures. Both end up on page one.
advisor.zh: 你发了两张干净的图。两张最终都被放在了第一页。

advisor.en: Say your own deadline comes first
advisor.zh: 解释自己文章的截稿更要紧

advisor.en: "Fair. Your paper matters more right now." You get your week back.
advisor.zh: “有道理。你的论文更重要。”你的这一周保住了。

advisor.en: {advisor} says "fine" in a way that is not quite fine.
advisor.zh: {advisor}回了句“行吧”。懂的都懂，这不太行。

advisor.en: A Brand-New Idea
advisor.zh: 一个全新的想法

advisor.en: {advisor} bursts into lab meeting with an exciting new idea. It's the idea you pitched last year, the one they called "not quite there".
advisor.zh: {advisor}冲进组会，带来一个激动人心的新想法。正是你去年提过，但被一句“还差点意思”毙掉的那个。

advisor.en: Say "I pitched that last year!"
advisor.zh: 直接说“这是我去年提的！”

advisor.en: {advisor} checks their notes and laughs. "Then you should lead it."
advisor.zh: {advisor}翻了翻笔记，笑了：“那就你来牵头吧。”

advisor.en: "Similar, but this version is different." It is not different.
advisor.zh: “有点像，但这个版本不一样。”并没有不一样。

advisor.en: Say "Great idea!" and smile
advisor.zh: 笑着说“好主意！”

advisor.en: You start a new folder for it. Your notes from last year are already inside.
advisor.zh: 你为它新建了一个文件夹。你去年的笔记已经在里面了。

advisor.en: Send them your old slides
advisor.zh: 把旧幻灯片发给导师

advisor.en: "Ha, you were early." Your slides from last year become the starting point.
advisor.zh: “哈，你早就想到了。”你去年的幻灯片成了起点。

advisor.en: Rescheduled Into Your Vacation
advisor.zh: 开会改到了假期里

advisor.en: {advisor} forgets your meeting and, to make up for it, moves it to the one week you'll be away.
advisor.zh: {advisor}忘了你们的会，为了弥补，贴心地把它挪到了你唯一不在的那一周。

advisor.en: Take the call from vacation
advisor.zh: 度假时接电话开会

advisor.en: You take the 12-minute call from a parking lot, and {advisor} seems pleased.
advisor.zh: 你坐在停车场开完了 12 分钟的电话会，{advisor}似乎挺满意。

advisor.en: Ask to move it again
advisor.zh: 请求再改个时间

advisor.en: "Oh! Of course. Enjoy your break." It moves to the week after.
advisor.zh: “哦！没问题。好好休息。”会挪到了再下一周。

advisor.en: It moves to the morning you fly back.
advisor.zh: 会挪到了你飞回来的那天早上。

advisor.en: Send a written update instead
advisor.zh: 改发邮件汇报进展

advisor.en: You send a tidy one-page update. {advisor} replies "perfect, enjoy!" and means it.
advisor.zh: 你发了一页满满当当的进展汇报。{advisor}回复“做得不错，玩得开心！”，而且是真心的。

advisor.en: Tomorrow's Guest Lecture
advisor.zh: 明天的客座讲课

advisor.en: {advisor} is stuck in another meeting. "Could you give my guest lecture tomorrow? The slides are mostly done."
advisor.zh: {advisor}被另一个会困住了。“明天的客座讲课你能替我上吗？幻灯片差不多做好了。”

advisor.en: Give it with their slides
advisor.zh: 用导师的幻灯片讲

advisor.en: The slides are from 2019, but you narrate them well. Two students ask for your email.
advisor.zh: 幻灯片是 2019 年的，但你讲得很好。有两个学生来要你的邮箱。

advisor.en: Slide 14 cites a model nobody has heard of. You improvise for ten long minutes.
advisor.zh: 第 14 页引用了一个你都没听说过的模型。你硬着头皮东拉西扯了漫长的十分钟。

advisor.en: Rebuild the slides tonight
advisor.zh: 今晚重做幻灯片

advisor.en: You give a crisp lecture built around your own work. {advisor} hears it went great.
advisor.zh: 你围绕自己的工作讲了一堂干脆利落的课。{advisor}听说讲得很好。

advisor.en: Say you can't this time
advisor.zh: 说这次去不了

advisor.en: The lecture is canceled. The class gets a free hour and seems thrilled.
advisor.zh: 课取消了。学生们白捡一小时，快乐得像放了假。

advisor.en: My Star Student
advisor.zh: 我的得意门生

advisor.en: At the {venue} reception in {city}, {advisor} introduces you to a famous researcher as "my star student". The famous researcher turns to you, expectantly.
advisor.zh: 在{city}的 {venue} 招待会上，{advisor}把你介绍给一位知名学者：“这是我的得意门生。”那位学者转过身来，满怀期待地看着你。

advisor.en: Pitch your work in one minute
advisor.zh: 一分钟介绍你的研究

advisor.en: They ask one sharp question, then for your paper. You've made a real contact.
advisor.zh: 对方问了一个犀利的问题，然后记下了你的论文标题。这次是真的搭上了线。

advisor.en: You say "basically" eleven times. They are very kind about it.
advisor.zh: 你说了十一次“基本上……”；对方非常包容。

advisor.en: Ask about their work instead
advisor.zh: 反过来问对方的研究

advisor.en: They talk for twenty minutes. You learn a lot and are remembered as a great listener.
advisor.zh: 对方讲了二十分钟。你学到很多，还留下了一个“很会倾听”的好印象。

advisor.en: Laugh: "Star is generous."
advisor.zh: 笑说“得意门生不敢当”

advisor.en: Everyone laughs, and {advisor} looks proud.
advisor.zh: 大家都笑了，{advisor}看起来很骄傲。

advisor.en: You're Running Reading Group
advisor.zh: 读书会归你了

advisor.en: "{player} will run reading group this semester," {advisor} announces. This is the first you've heard of it.
advisor.zh: “这学期的读书会由 {player} 负责。”{advisor}宣布。这事你本人也是刚知道。

advisor.en: Run it properly
advisor.zh: 认真办

advisor.en: You pick good papers and bring snacks, and attendance doubles.
advisor.zh: 你仔细挑选了论文，还带了零食，参加人数翻了一倍。

advisor.en: Make it a rotation
advisor.zh: 改成轮流主讲

advisor.en: Everyone takes a week, so you only present twice.
advisor.zh: 每人轮一周，你只讲了两次。

advisor.en: Nobody signs up. You present for six weeks straight.
advisor.zh: 没人报名。你连讲了六周。

advisor.en: Pick only papers for your project
advisor.zh: 夹带私货，只选项目相关的

advisor.en: Every paper is about your project. The lab learns a lot about it, and so do you.
advisor.zh: 每篇论文都和你的项目有关。组里对它了解了很多，你也是。

advisor.en: Weekly Progress Reports
advisor.zh: 周报

advisor.en: {advisor} wants a written progress report every week from now on. "Just a few bullet points. Every Friday."
advisor.zh: {advisor}说以后每周交一份周报。“列几条要点就行，每周五发我。”空气里飘来一股班味。

advisor.en: Write them every Friday
advisor.zh: 每周五按时写

advisor.en: Writing down what you did turns out to be useful. Writing down what you didn't do, less so.
advisor.zh: 把做了什么写下来，原来挺有用。把没做什么写下来，就没那么有用了。

advisor.en: Turn your notes into the report
advisor.zh: 直接把笔记改成报告

advisor.en: Your lab notebook becomes the report, and it takes ten minutes a week.
advisor.zh: 你的实验记录本直接变成了报告，每周只花十分钟。

advisor.en: Your notes say "fixed thing" four times. {advisor} asks which thing.
advisor.zh: 你的笔记里写了四次“改了点东西”。{advisor}问是哪个东西。

advisor.en: Propose a shared progress doc
advisor.zh: 提议用共享进展文档

advisor.en: {advisor} likes it. Nobody reads it but you, which helps more than you expect.
advisor.zh: {advisor}很喜欢，只是除了你没人看它，但这比你想的更有用。

advisor.en: A Very Motivated Undergrad
advisor.zh: 本科卷王来了

advisor.en: {advisor} asks you to mentor {mentee}, a new undergrad who is "very motivated". {mentee} has already emailed you twice.
advisor.zh: {advisor}让你带 {mentee}，一个“干劲十足”的新本科生。{mentee} 已经给你发了两封邮件。

advisor.en: Give them a real subproject
advisor.zh: 给对方一个真正的子项目

advisor.en: You write {mentee} a two-page plan. Explaining your project makes you understand it better.
advisor.zh: 你给 {mentee} 写了一份两页的计划。给别人讲自己的项目的过程反而让你对项目理解得更透了。

advisor.en: Start them on reading
advisor.zh: 先让对方读论文

advisor.en: You send {mentee} five papers. They read all five by Tuesday and come back with good questions.
advisor.zh: 你给 {mentee} 发了五篇论文。到周二对方就全读完了，还带着一堆问题来找你。

advisor.en: Suggest {labmate} instead
advisor.zh: 推荐 {labmate} 来带

advisor.en: {labmate} is delighted. They've wanted a mentee for months.
advisor.zh: {labmate} 很高兴，几个月来一直想带个学生。

advisor.en: {labmate} is swamped, so {mentee} becomes yours anyway, a week late.
advisor.zh: {labmate} 忙得不可开交，所以 {mentee} 最后还是归你带，只是拖了一周。

advisor.en: One Inspiring Keynote
advisor.zh: 报告听上头了

advisor.en: {advisor} comes back from one inspiring keynote and wants {project} to go in a whole new direction. "Everything is about this now."
advisor.zh: {advisor}听了一场振奋人心的主旨报告回来，想让 {project} 彻底换个方向。“现在一切都要围绕这个方向。”

advisor.en: Pivot {project}
advisor.zh: 给 {project} 转方向

advisor.en: You're back at the idea stage, with half your novelty and a clean whiteboard.
advisor.zh: 你回到了想法阶段，新颖性只剩一半，白板倒是干干净净。

advisor.en: Add one experiment in that direction
advisor.zh: 往那个方向加一个实验

advisor.en: One small experiment satisfies the keynote energy, and it actually adds something.
advisor.zh: 一个小实验就接住了导师听完报告的那股劲儿，而且确实有点用。

advisor.en: Wait a week and see
advisor.zh: 等一周看看

advisor.en: A week later, {advisor} has moved on to a different keynote.
advisor.zh: 一周后，{advisor}又被另一场主旨报告圈粉了。

advisor.en: A week later, they've watched the keynote twice more and are disappointed in you.
advisor.zh: 一周后，导师又把那场报告看了两遍，对你有点失望。

advisor.en: Caught in the Middle
advisor.zh: 夹心饼干

advisor.en: {advisor} wants {project} framed as a methods paper. Your collaborator wants a findings paper. Both email you, separately, within the same minute.
advisor.zh: {advisor}想把 {project} 写成方法论文，你的合作者想写成发现型论文。两人在同一分钟内分别给你发了邮件。

advisor.en: Side with your advisor
advisor.zh: 站导师这边

advisor.en: Methods it is. The collaborator goes quiet for a week.
advisor.zh: 那就写方法。合作者沉默了一周。

advisor.en: Side with the collaborator
advisor.zh: 站合作者那边

advisor.en: Findings it is. {advisor} agrees, slowly, and remembers.
advisor.zh: 那就写发现。{advisor}慢慢点头同意，然后记在了小本本上。

advisor.en: Draft both framings
advisor.zh: 两种写法都写

advisor.en: You write two introductions. Everyone picks the second one, which neither of them proposed.
advisor.zh: 你写了两版引言。大家都选了第二版，而那是他们俩谁都没提过的。

advisor.en: Get them both on one call
advisor.zh: 拉两人开个电话会

advisor.en: Twenty minutes later they agree, and each thinks it was their idea.
advisor.zh: 二十分钟后两人达成一致，而且都觉得是自己的主意。

advisor.en: The call runs an hour. You leave with three framings instead of two.
advisor.zh: 电话开了一小时。你带走的写法从两种变成了三种。

advisor.en: "sounds good"
advisor.zh: “挺好的”

advisor.en: You send {advisor} a 2,000-word email laying out three options, with pros and cons for each. They reply "sounds good".
advisor.zh: 你给 {advisor}发了一封 2000 字的小作文，列出三个方案，每个都写了优缺点。导师回复：“挺好的。”

advisor.en: Pick the option you liked
advisor.zh: 选你喜欢的方案

advisor.en: You go with option B. Nobody objects, possibly because nobody read option A.
advisor.zh: 你选了方案 B。没人反对，可能是因为没人读过方案 A。

advisor.en: Ask "Which one?"
advisor.zh: 追问“哪一个？”

advisor.en: They call you, and you get ten genuinely useful minutes.
advisor.zh: 导师给你打了电话，你得到了实实在在有用的十分钟。

advisor.en: They reply "sounds good" again.
advisor.zh: 导师又回了一句“挺好的”。

advisor.en: Send a three-line version
advisor.zh: 发个三行精简版

advisor.en: The three-line version gets a real answer in four minutes.
advisor.zh: 三行版四分钟就换来了一个真正的答复。

advisor.en: Comments on Version 2
advisor.zh: 第 2 版的修改意见

advisor.en: {advisor} finally sends comments on your draft of {project}. They are on version 2, and you are on version 5.
advisor.zh: {advisor}终于发来了对 {project} 草稿的意见。导师看的是第 2 版，你已经写到第 5 版了。

advisor.en: Map their comments onto v5
advisor.zh: 把意见对应到 v5

advisor.en: Half the comments are already fixed. The other half are good.
advisor.zh: 一半的意见已经改完了。另一半倒提得很好。

advisor.en: Reply "Fixed in v5!"
advisor.zh: 回复“v5 里已经改了！”

advisor.en: "Oh, great." You suspect v5 will be read sometime around v8.
advisor.zh: “哦，太好了。”你怀疑 v5 大概要到 v8 前后才会被读到。

advisor.en: Ask them to read v5 now
advisor.zh: 请导师现在就看 v5

advisor.en: They read v5 that night. The comments are sharp and on time.
advisor.zh: 导师当晚就读了 v5。意见一针见血，而且来得及时。

advisor.en: "Will do!" They do not.
advisor.zh: “好的！”然后就没有然后了。

advisor.en: Sabbatical Abroad
advisor.zh: 出国学术休假

advisor.en: {advisor} is taking a sabbatical abroad for the next few months. "Nothing changes! We'll just meet at 6 am your time."
advisor.zh: {advisor}接下来几个月要出国学术休假。“一切照旧！我们就改成你那边早上 6 点开会。”

advisor.en: Set three alarms
advisor.zh: 定三个闹钟

advisor.en: You buy a second coffee maker. The first 6 am meeting goes fine, mostly.
advisor.zh: 你又买了一台咖啡机。第一次早上 6 点的会，基本没翻车。

advisor.en: Propose written updates instead
advisor.zh: 提议改成书面汇报

advisor.en: {advisor} agrees: a written update each week, plus one call a month.
advisor.zh: {advisor}同意了：每周一份书面汇报，外加每月一次通话。

advisor.en: "Let's try 6 am first and see." You set your alarm.
advisor.zh: “先试试 6 点开会再说吧。”你定好了闹钟。

advisor.en: Say 6 am is your best hour
advisor.zh: 说 6 点正是你的黄金时间

advisor.en: Early Bird
advisor.zh: 晨型人

advisor.en: You're sharpest at dawn anyway. {advisor} is impressed by how awake you are.
advisor.zh: 反正你天一亮脑子最清楚。{advisor}很惊讶你怎么这么精神。

advisor.en: Stay up until 6 am instead
advisor.zh: 干脆熬到早上 6 点

advisor.en: Night Owl
advisor.zh: 夜猫子

advisor.en: For you, 6 am is the end of the day. The meetings are oddly relaxed.
advisor.zh: 对你来说，早上 6 点是一天的结束。这些会开得出奇地轻松。

advisor.en: The 6 am Call
advisor.zh: 早上 6 点的电话会

advisor.en: You join the call at 5:58 am. {advisor} is eating lunch in the sun and wants to tell you about their host lab.
advisor.zh: 你在早上 5:58 加入通话。{advisor}正在阳光下吃午饭，想跟你聊聊这次访问的实验室。

advisor.en: Join their lab's meeting too
advisor.zh: 顺便参加那边的组会

advisor.en: You present to a lab you've never met, at dawn. Two of them email you afterward.
advisor.zh: 天刚亮，你就给一个素不相识的实验室做了报告。会后有两个人给你发了邮件。

advisor.en: Keep it to your project
advisor.zh: 只聊你的项目

advisor.en: You get exactly the feedback you need, then sleep for another hour.
advisor.zh: 你拿到了正好需要的反馈，然后倒头又睡了一个小时。

advisor.en: Ask to visit for a week
advisor.zh: 申请过去访问一周

advisor.en: "Yes! I'll find the travel money." You start looking at flights.
advisor.zh: “好啊！差旅费我来想办法。”你开始看机票了。

advisor.en: "I'd love that, but the budget is tight this year."
advisor.zh: “我很想，但今年预算紧。”

advisor.en: A Week Abroad
advisor.zh: 海外一周

advisor.en: You spend a week in {advisor}'s host lab abroad. The coffee is better, and so is the whiteboard.
advisor.zh: 你在 {advisor}访问的海外实验室待了一周。咖啡更好，白板也更好。

advisor.en: Give a talk to their lab
advisor.zh: 给那边的组做报告

advisor.en: The questions are great and lunch runs long. They invite you to come back.
advisor.zh: 提问很精彩，午饭吃了很久。他们邀请你以后有机会再来。

advisor.en: The projector fights you for ten minutes. The discussion after is still good.
advisor.zh: 投影仪跟你较劲了十分钟。之后的讨论还是很不错。

advisor.en: Work side by side with {advisor}
advisor.zh: 和 {advisor}并肩干活

advisor.en: With real daytime meetings, you get more done in a week than in the last two months.
advisor.zh: 白天能正常开会，你一周干的活比过去两个月还多。

advisor.en: Explore the city on the weekend
advisor.zh: 周末逛逛这座城市

advisor.en: You eat everything and come home with two ideas and a fridge magnet.
advisor.zh: 你特种兵式吃遍全城，带着两个想法和一块冰箱贴回了家。

advisor.en: Back From Sabbatical
advisor.zh: 休假归来

advisor.en: {advisor} is back from sabbatical, full of ideas, with a small souvenir for everyone. Your meetings return to a human hour.
advisor.zh: {advisor}休假回来了，满脑子想法，还给每个人带了小纪念品。你们的会终于回到了正常人的时间。

advisor.en: Pitch an idea from the trip
advisor.zh: 提一个这趟旅程里的想法

advisor.en: One idea sticks. {advisor} wants a paper on it.
advisor.zh: 有一个想法获得了认同。{advisor}想就此写篇论文。

advisor.en: "Interesting! Let's revisit." It is never revisited.
advisor.zh: “有意思！回头再聊。”再也没有回头。

advisor.en: Enjoy your first 10 am meeting
advisor.zh: 享受第一次上午 10 点的会

advisor.en: You sleep until 8, like a person.
advisor.zh: 你一觉睡到 8 点，活得像个人了。

advisor.en: Ask for the people they met
advisor.zh: 打听导师这趟认识的人

advisor.en: You get forty minutes of stories and three introductions to people you should know.
advisor.zh: 你听了四十分钟的故事，还被引荐给了三位你该认识的人。

advisor.en: By Friday?
advisor.zh: 周五前？

advisor.en: {advisor} asks if you could put together slides about your project for a funder visit, by Friday.
advisor.zh: {advisor}问你能不能在周五前做一份介绍你项目的幻灯片，资助方要来访。

advisor.en: {advisor} needs two paragraphs on your project for a grant renewal. "Nothing fancy. By Friday?"
advisor.zh: {advisor}的基金续期需要两段介绍你项目的文字。“不用太讲究。周五前可以吗？”

advisor.en: Drop everything and do it well
advisor.zh: 放下一切，好好做

advisor.en: Your slides make it into the meeting, and your advisor mentions your name twice.
advisor.zh: 你的幻灯片上了会，老板还两次提到了你的名字。

advisor.en: Do a quick version
advisor.zh: 先糊弄一版

advisor.en: It's good enough. Your advisor polishes it at midnight and doesn't mention it.
advisor.zh: 够用了。导师半夜帮你润色了一遍，什么也没说。

advisor.en: Ask for until next Wednesday
advisor.zh: 申请宽限到下周三

advisor.en: "Sure, Wednesday works." You could have just asked all along.
advisor.zh: “行啊，周三也可以。”早知道一开始就问了。

advisor.en: Would You Come With Me?
advisor.zh: 你愿意跟我走吗？

advisor.en: {advisor} closes the office door. Another university has made them an offer, a big one. "Nothing is decided. But if I go, would you come with me?"
advisor.zh: {advisor}关上办公室的门。另一所大学给导师抛来了橄榄枝，听说给得很到位。“还没定。但如果我走，你愿意跟我一起吗？”

advisor.en: Say you'd come with them
advisor.zh: 说你愿意跟着走

advisor.en: {advisor} looks relieved. That night you look up rents in a city you've never visited.
advisor.zh: {advisor}看起来松了口气。当晚你就开始查一座从没去过的城市的房租。

advisor.en: Say you'd rather stay here
advisor.zh: 说你更想留下

advisor.en: "That's fair. We'd make it work either way." You tell your roommate you're not going anywhere.
advisor.zh: “可以理解。不管怎样我们都能安排好。”你告诉室友，你哪儿也不去。

advisor.en: Ask for a few weeks to think
advisor.zh: 请几周时间考虑

advisor.en: "Of course." You think about it on the bus and through two entire seminars.
advisor.zh: “当然。”你坐公交时在想，整整两场讲座也都在想。

advisor.en: The Counteroffer
advisor.zh: 挽留条件

advisor.en: The department makes {advisor} a counteroffer. For two weeks the lab reads every closed door like tea leaves. Then {advisor} asks what you honestly think.
advisor.zh: 系里给 {advisor}开出了挽留条件。整整两周，组里的人把每一扇关着的门都当成卦象来解读。然后 {advisor}问你真实的想法。

advisor.en: Tell them to take the offer
advisor.zh: 劝导师接受 offer

advisor.en: "Thank you. That helps more than you know." They accept the new job the next morning.
advisor.zh: “谢谢你。这比你想的更有帮助。”第二天一早，导师接受了新工作。

advisor.en: Say you hope they stay
advisor.zh: 说你希望导师留下

advisor.en: They stay. The counteroffer comes with a bigger lab, and they say your answer tipped it.
advisor.zh: 导师留下了。挽留条件里有一个更大的实验室，导师说是你的回答让自己改了主意。

advisor.en: "I hear you. I still think I have to go." They take the offer, and promise you won't be left behind.
advisor.zh: “我明白。但我还是觉得我得走。”导师接受了 offer，并保证不会把你丢下。

advisor.en: Moving Week
advisor.zh: 搬家周

advisor.en: You follow {advisor} to their new university, where you get a new badge and an empty lab that echoes.
advisor.zh: 你跟着 {advisor}去了新学校，领到一张新工牌和一间空得能听见回声的实验室。

advisor.en: Set up the new lab yourself
advisor.zh: 亲手搭起新实验室

advisor.en: You label every machine and get every login working. {advisor} introduces you as the lab's co-founder.
advisor.zh: 你给每台机器贴好标签，搞定了每一个账号登录。{advisor}介绍你时说你是实验室的联合创始人。

advisor.en: Meet the new department
advisor.zh: 认识新院系

advisor.en: After twelve coffees in five days, you know who has the good GPUs and who has the good snacks.
advisor.zh: 五天喝了十二次咖啡，你摸清了谁手里有卡，谁抽屉里有零食。

advisor.en: Live out of boxes and keep working
advisor.zh: 住在纸箱堆里继续干活

advisor.en: Your desk is a box, and so is your chair. Your experiments don't notice the move, but your back does.
advisor.zh: 你的桌子是个纸箱，椅子也是。你的实验没察觉到搬家，但你的腰察觉到了。

advisor.en: Advising From Afar
advisor.zh: 远程指导

advisor.en: {advisor} moves to their new university, and you stay. Your meetings are on video now, and a professor down the hall agrees to sign your forms.
advisor.zh: {advisor}去了新学校，你留了下来。你们改成视频开会，走廊那头的一位教授答应帮你签各种表格。

advisor.en: Set a fixed weekly video call
advisor.zh: 固定每周视频会

advisor.en: You meet Thursdays at 10, with an agenda sent the night before. It works better than the hallway chats ever did.
advisor.zh: 你们每周四 10 点开会，前一晚发议程。比以前在走廊上聊的效果还好。

advisor.en: Ask the local professor to co-advise
advisor.zh: 请本校那位教授联合指导

advisor.en: They say yes. Now you get twice the comments, and someone nearby when {advisor} is hard to reach.
advisor.zh: 对方答应了。现在你收到的意见翻倍，而且 {advisor}联系不上的时候，身边也有人可找。

advisor.en: They're happy to sign forms, and only forms. You'll make the video calls work.
advisor.zh: 对方乐意签表格，但也只签表格。视频会你得自己想办法开好。

advisor.en: Enjoy the quiet
advisor.zh: 享受清静

advisor.en: Nobody drops by your desk unannounced anymore. You get a lot done, and you and {advisor} drift a little.
advisor.zh: 再也没人不打招呼就跑到你桌前了。你效率很高，和 {advisor}却渐渐疏远了一点。

career.en: Invert a Binary Tree
career.zh: 手撕二叉树

career.en: Your internship interview at {company} is for a research role on language models. The first question: "Let's warm up. Invert a binary tree."
career.zh: 你在 {company} 面的是大模型方向的研究实习。第一题：“先热个身，翻转一个二叉树吧。”

career.en: Invert the binary tree
career.zh: 翻转这个二叉树

career.en: You write six clean lines and handle the edge cases. The interviewer relaxes and asks about your research.
career.zh: 六行代码一气呵成，边界情况一个没漏。面试官神色一松，开始问你的研究。

career.en: You invert it twice, which gives back the original tree. The interviewer says "interesting" and writes something down.
career.zh: 你翻转了两次，二叉树完美复原。面试官说了句“有意思”，低头记了点什么。

career.en: Ask clarifying questions first
career.zh: 先把题目问清楚

career.en: Your questions turn it into a conversation. You solve it slowly, but they like how you think.
career.zh: 你的提问让面试变成了聊天。题解得有点慢，但对方很欣赏你的思路。

career.en: You ask so many questions that time runs out before you write any code.
career.zh: 你问了太多问题，一行代码还没写，时间就到了。

career.en: Solve it fast, then pivot to research
career.zh: 速速解题，转聊研究

career.en: You solve it and steer the talk to your paper, while the interviewer glances at the clock.
career.zh: 你解完题就把话题往自己的论文上带，面试官瞄了一眼时钟。

career.en: Your Mentor Has Left the Building
career.zh: Mentor 已退出群聊

career.en: In week two of your internship at {company}, your mentor announces they are moving to another team, effective Friday. Your project doc still says "TBD with mentor".
career.zh: 在 {company} 实习的第二周，你的 mentor 宣布要转去别的组，周五生效。你的项目文档里还写着“待与 mentor 确定”。

career.en: Find a new mentor yourself
career.zh: 自己找个新 mentor

career.en: A senior researcher two desks over adopts you, and turns out to be better at this than your first mentor.
career.zh: 隔两个工位的一位资深研究员收留了你，结果带得比原来的 mentor 还好。

career.en: Everyone is "happy to chat", but nobody is happy to mentor. You spend a week in limbo.
career.zh: 人人都“很乐意聊聊”，但没人乐意带你。你在三不管地带晃荡了一周。

career.en: Scope the project yourself
career.zh: 自己给自己立项

career.en: You write your own project plan, and your manager approves it without reading it.
career.zh: 你自己写了项目计划，经理看都没看就批了。

career.en: Ask your old mentor for weekly chats
career.zh: 约前 mentor 每周聊聊

career.en: They agree to a 30-minute call every Thursday from their new team.
career.zh: 对方答应每周四从新组抽 30 分钟跟你通个电话。

career.en: Footnote 3
career.zh: 脚注 3

career.en: Your internship project at {company} ships. The press release thanks "the team". Your name is in footnote 3, spelled correctly.
career.zh: 你在 {company} 的实习项目上线了。新闻稿感谢了“团队”。你的名字出现在脚注 3 里，拼写无误。

career.en: Add it to your CV
career.zh: 写进简历

career.en: "Shipped to millions of users." It is one line on your CV, and recruiters read that line first.
career.zh: “上线服务数百万用户。”简历上就这一行，HR 却第一眼就看它。

career.en: Ask about a return offer
career.zh: 问问转正 offer

career.en: Your manager says they were about to bring it up. A return offer is on the table.
career.zh: 经理说正打算跟你提这事。转正 offer 已经摆上桌了。

career.en: "Let's revisit after headcount planning." Nobody knows when that is.
career.zh: “等 Head Count 定下来再说。”没人知道那是哪天。

career.en: Pitch a paper on the project
career.zh: 提议把项目写成论文

career.en: Legal approves a short workshop paper. People start citing it before you're back on campus.
career.zh: 法务批了一篇 workshop 短文。你还没回学校，就已经有人开始引用了。

career.en: Legal says the paper can come out "after the next product cycle", which could mean next year.
career.zh: 法务说论文可以“等下个产品周期之后”再发。翻译成人话：至少得到明年。

career.en: Fellowship!
career.zh: 奖学金到手！

career.en: The fellowship is yours. For a whole year you don't have to TA or grade, and your calendar suddenly has room in it.
career.zh: 奖学金是你的了。整整一年不用当助教、不用改作业，日历突然空出了一大块。

career.en: Put the time into a bold idea
career.zh: 梭哈一个大胆的想法

career.en: You start the project you have been too busy to start, knowing it might not work.
career.zh: 你终于开始做那个一直忙得没空碰的项目，明知道它可能做不成。

career.en: Catch up on sleep first
career.zh: 先把觉补回来

career.en: You sleep properly for two weeks and are sharper than you have been since orientation.
career.zh: 你好好睡了两周，脑子是入学以来最清醒的。

career.en: Celebrate with the lab
career.zh: 请全组吃顿好的

career.en: You buy the lab dinner. {labmate} toasts "to no grading". A few labmates look envious.
career.zh: 你请全组吃火锅。{labmate} 举杯：“敬不用改作业！”几个同门当场酸了。

career.en: Fellowship Feedback
career.zh: 奖学金评审意见

career.en: The fellowship results are out, and you didn't get it. The reviewer comments come too. One says "too ambitious", another "not ambitious enough", and a third calls it "incremental".
career.zh: 奖学金结果出来了，你没拿到。评审意见也一并发来：一个说“太有野心”，一个说“不够有野心”，第三个说“创新性不足”。

career.en: Look for the useful critique
career.zh: 从意见里淘点干货

career.en: Two comments are actually useful. You fold them into next year's research statement.
career.zh: 有两条意见确实有用。你把它们写进了明年的研究陈述。

career.en: Vent to your cohort over dinner
career.zh: 约同届吃饭吐槽

career.en: Half your cohort got the same three comments. Dinner turns into a dramatic reading.
career.zh: 同届一半的人收到了一模一样的三条意见。晚饭变成了评审意见诗朗诵大会。

career.en: Start next year's application today
career.zh: 今天就开始写明年的申请

career.en: You open a new document while you're still annoyed. It is a surprisingly productive mood.
career.zh: 你带着一肚子气新建了文档。化悲愤为生产力，效率居然出奇地高。

career.en: Sixty Cover Letters
career.zh: 六十封求职信

career.en: It's faculty application season, and each of 60 openings wants a custom cover letter plus two statements. You have already mixed up two department names.
career.zh: 教职申请季到了，60 个职位每个都要一封定制求职信，外加两份陈述。你已经把两个院系的名字写混了。

career.en: Write 60 truly custom letters
career.zh: 认真定制 60 封信

career.en: Each letter names the faculty you would work with. It takes three weeks and part of your soul.
career.zh: 每封信都点名了你想合作的老师。花了三周，外加一小块灵魂。

career.en: Use one template plus a custom paragraph
career.zh: 套模板，再加一段定制

career.en: The letters are good and go out on time. You triple-check every department name.
career.zh: 信写得不错，也按时发了出去。每个院系的名字你都核对了三遍。

career.en: Apply only to your best 25
career.zh: 只投最合适的 25 个

career.en: You put more care into fewer letters, and your stress level survives application season.
career.zh: 信少了，每封都更用心。整个申请季，你的心态居然没崩。

career.en: Letter Pending
career.zh: 推荐信未到

career.en: Three application portals show the same red status: "Letter of recommendation: not received." The deadlines were yesterday. The missing letter is from {advisor}.
career.zh: 三个申请系统亮着同一行红字：“推荐信：未收到。”截止日期是昨天。没交的那封来自 {advisor}。

career.en: Send {advisor} a gentle reminder
career.zh: 委婉地催一下 {advisor}

career.en: {advisor} apologizes and uploads all three within the hour. Two committees say late letters are fine.
career.zh: {advisor}连声道歉，一小时内把三封全传了。两个招聘委员会说晚交没关系。

career.en: {advisor} replies "on it!" and uploads one. The other two arrive next week.
career.zh: {advisor}秒回“马上！”，然后传了一封。另外两封下周才到。

career.en: Send a page of talking points
career.zh: 发一页要点过去

career.en: You send a one-page summary of your work. {advisor} uses it, and the letters go out the next morning.
career.zh: 你发了一页纸的工作总结。{advisor}照着用了，推荐信第二天早上就发了出去。

career.en: Email the search committees yourself
career.zh: 自己给招聘委员会发邮件

career.en: Two of the three committees reply kindly. The third portal has no contact address, only a FAQ.
career.zh: 三个委员会里有两个回得很客气。第三个系统没有联系邮箱，只有一页 FAQ。

career.en: Equity and a Ping-Pong Table
career.zh: 期权和乒乓球桌

career.en: A startup founder messages you: "We'd love you as a founding researcher. Generous equity, a ping-pong table, free snacks." The word "salary" does not appear.
career.zh: 一位创业公司创始人给你发消息：“诚邀你成为创始研究员。丰厚期权、乒乓球桌、免费零食。”通篇没出现“工资”两个字。

career.en: Hear them out
career.zh: 听听对方怎么说

career.en: The pitch is wild and a little convincing. You add startups to your search, just in case.
career.zh: 对方画的饼很大，闻着还有点香。你把创业公司也加进了求职清单，以防万一。

career.en: Ask about the salary directly
career.zh: 直接问工资

career.en: They name a real number: below big tech, above what you feared. You are more interested than you expected.
career.zh: 对方报了个实打实的数字：比大厂低，但比你估计的高。你比自己预想的还要心动。

career.en: "We think about compensation holistically." The conversation ends there.
career.zh: “薪酬方面，我们是综合考量的。”天就这么聊死了。

career.en: Decline and stay on your track
career.zh: 婉拒，坚持原计划

career.en: You wish them luck. They thank you and ask if you know anyone else.
career.zh: 你祝对方好运。对方道了谢，又问你有没有认识的人可以推荐。

career.en: Wait, I Applied There?
career.zh: 等等，我投过这家？

career.en: A job-talk invitation arrives from a school you had completely forgotten you applied to. You search your sent mail to see what you promised them.
career.zh: 一所你完全忘了投过的学校发来 job talk 邀请。你翻遍已发送邮件，想看看自己当初跟人家许诺了什么。

career.en: Accept and study the department
career.zh: 接受，好好研究这个系

career.en: You read every faculty page and three of their papers. On the visit, you sound like you've wanted this job for years.
career.zh: 你看遍了每位老师的主页，还读了他们三篇论文。到了现场，你听起来像是惦记这份工作好多年了。

career.en: Accept and give your usual talk
career.zh: 接受，讲老一套

career.en: Your usual talk lands just as well. The search chair calls it "refreshingly clear".
career.zh: 老一套照样好使。招聘委员会主席说你讲得“清晰得让人耳目一新”。

career.en: Your talk mentions collaborating with a research center they closed years ago.
career.zh: 你的报告里说要和一个研究中心合作，可那个中心好几年前就关了。

career.en: Decline politely
career.zh: 礼貌婉拒

career.en: You trade a flight for a free weekend. After a small pang, you feel relieved.
career.zh: 你用一趟航班换来一个空闲的周末。心里小小失落了一下，然后松了口气。

career.en: Twelve One-on-Ones
career.zh: 十二场车轮战

career.en: Campus visit: breakfast with the search chair, twelve 30-minute one-on-ones, your job talk, then dinner. Every single person asks, "So, tell me about your research."
career.zh: 校园面试：和招聘委员会主席吃早饭，十二场 30 分钟的单独会面，你的 job talk，然后是晚饭。每个人都会问：“那么，说说你的研究吧。”

career.en: Be fully on for all twelve
career.zh: 十二场全程满电

career.en: You give twelve slightly different versions of your pitch, and everyone loves you. You fall asleep in your dinner clothes.
career.zh: 你讲了十二个略有不同的版本，所有人都很喜欢你。你穿着赴宴的衣服就睡着了。

career.en: Ask about their work instead
career.zh: 反过来问对方的研究

career.en: You've read their papers and ask sharp questions. Half the meetings run over, happily.
career.zh: 你读过他们的论文，问题问得很犀利。一半的会面都聊超了时，宾主尽欢。

career.en: You mix up two professors' papers. One of them is very gracious about it.
career.zh: 你把两位教授的论文搞混了。其中一位非常大度。

career.en: Save your energy for the talk
career.zh: 留着精力讲报告

career.en: You keep the one-on-ones short and give a sharp job talk. Dinner is quiet, but fine.
career.zh: 你把单独会面都控制得很短，job talk 讲得干脆利落。晚饭有点安静，但还行。

career.en: One Week Apart
career.zh: offer 时间差

career.en: One place wants your answer by next Friday. The place you like more will decide a week after that. Both say, "Take all the time you need."
career.zh: 一家要你下周五前答复。你更想去的那家，要再晚一周才出结果。两家都说：“不着急，慢慢考虑。”

career.en: Ask the first place for more time
career.zh: 请第一家多宽限几天

career.en: They give you two extra weeks. Now the dates line up.
career.zh: 对方多给了你两周。这下时间对上了。

career.en: "We can't extend, but we really hope you'll join!" You still have until Friday.
career.zh: “没法延期，但我们真心希望你能来！”期限还是周五。

career.en: Ask the second place to decide sooner
career.zh: 催第二家早点定

career.en: Your email is polite and clear. They move their decision up by a week.
career.zh: 你的邮件礼貌又清楚。对方把决定提前了一周。

career.en: They say they will "try", and then they don't.
career.zh: 对方说会“尽量”，然后就没有然后了。

career.en: Ask {advisor} what they would do
career.zh: 问问 {advisor}会怎么选

career.en: {advisor} tells you which one they would pick and, more usefully, why. You feel calmer about either.
career.zh: {advisor}告诉你会选哪家，更有用的是讲了为什么。现在不管选哪家，你都踏实多了。

career.en: A Famous Lab Writes Back
career.zh: 大牛组来信了

career.en: The head of a famous lab emails: they liked your talk and might have a postdoc opening. Could you chat on Thursday? Your heart rate disagrees with your calendar.
career.zh: 一位知名实验室的负责人发来邮件：很喜欢你的报告，可能有个博士后位置，周四能聊聊吗？你的日历说有空，你的心跳说没准备好。

career.en: Take the call and prepare hard
career.zh: 接下电话，拼命准备

career.en: You read their last ten papers. The call runs long and ends with "let's stay in touch". From them, that means something.
career.zh: 你读完了对方最近的十篇论文。电话聊超了时，最后对方说“保持联系”。从这位嘴里说出来，这话是有分量的。

career.en: Ask {advisor} what they know
career.zh: 向 {advisor}打听一下

career.en: {advisor} knows them well and makes a call of their own. You go into Thursday with an ally.
career.zh: {advisor}跟对方很熟，亲自打了个电话。周四你是带着援军去的。

career.en: {advisor} says, "They work their postdocs very hard." That is all they say.
career.zh: {advisor}说：“他们家博士后很辛苦的。”然后就再没多说一个字。

career.en: Keep it as a plan B
career.zh: 留着当备胎

career.en: You reply warmly and keep it in your back pocket while you focus on your main search.
career.zh: 你热情地回了信，把这条路揣进兜里，继续专心主线求职。

career.en: Employee #4
career.zh: 4 号员工

career.en: {labmate} pulls you aside: they are leaving to start a company, they just raised a small seed round, and they want you as employee number four. "You'd own a real piece of it."
career.zh: {labmate} 把你拉到一边：要离开组里去创业了，刚拿到一小笔种子轮，想让你当 4 号员工。“你能拿到实打实的股份。”

career.en: Say you're interested
career.zh: 表示感兴趣

career.en: {labmate} is thrilled. You agree to talk details once you're on the job market.
career.zh: {labmate} 激动坏了。你们约好等你开始求职时再细聊。

career.en: Ask to see the numbers first
career.zh: 先要份商业计划书

career.en: The plan makes sense. {labmate} respects the questions and keeps a spot open for you.
career.zh: 计划挺靠谱。{labmate} 很认可你提的问题，给你留了个位置。

career.en: The plan is one slide with a hockey-stick curve on it. You say you'll think about it.
career.zh: 整个计划就一页 PPT，上面画着一条一飞冲天的增长曲线。你说你再考虑考虑。

career.en: Decline, but offer to advise
career.zh: 婉拒，但愿意当顾问

career.en: You'll review their model evaluations for free. {labmate} is a little disappointed, but grateful.
career.zh: 你答应免费帮忙看模型评测。{labmate} 有点失望，但也很感激。

career.en: A Starter Allocation
career.zh: 新手大礼包

career.en: On day one at {company}, you get a GPU quota bigger than everything your lab has used in five years. The onboarding doc calls it "a starter allocation".
career.zh: 在 {company} 的第一天，你拿到的 GPU 配额比你们组五年用过的加起来还多。入职文档管这叫“基础配额”。

career.en: Run every ablation you ever dreamed of
career.zh: 把梦想中的消融实验全跑一遍

career.en: You launch two hundred runs by Friday and learn more about scaling in a week than in two years of queueing.
career.zh: 到周五你已经炼了两百炉丹。一周学到的 scaling 知识，比排了两年队学到的还多。

career.en: Plan runs as if GPUs were scarce
career.zh: 精打细算地用 GPU

career.en: Your mentor is impressed by how little compute you waste, and slightly confused by it.
career.zh: 你的 mentor 对你这么省算力印象深刻，但也有点不太理解。

career.en: Send the lab a screenshot
career.zh: 截图发到组群

career.en: The lab chat goes quiet for a long minute. Then {labmate} replies with one crying emoji.
career.zh: 组群里沉默了好一会儿。然后 {labmate} 回了一个大哭的表情。

career.en: Pending Legal Review
career.zh: 法务审核中

career.en: Your internship paper at {company} is finished, but legal review flagged "possible product implications". The next review slot is in eleven weeks.
career.zh: 你在 {company} 的实习论文写完了，但法务审核标记了“可能涉及产品”。下一个审核档期在十一周后。

career.en: Cut anything that sounds like a product
career.zh: 删掉一切像产品的内容

career.en: Every product name becomes "a deployed system". Legal approves a thinner, vaguer paper, and it's out.
career.zh: 所有产品名都改成了“某已部署系统”。法务批准了一篇更薄、更含糊的论文，总算发出去了。

career.en: Ask your manager to escalate
career.zh: 请经理往上推一推

career.en: Your manager knows someone in legal. The paper clears in a week, untouched.
career.zh: 经理在法务有熟人。论文一周就过了，一个字没改。

career.en: The escalation lands in the same queue, one slot lower.
career.zh: 升级后的请求进了同一个队列，还往后排了一位。

career.en: Let it wait and enjoy the summer
career.zh: 先放着，享受夏天

career.en: The paper goes into a folder called "someday". Your weekends come back for the rest of the internship.
career.zh: 论文进了一个叫“有空再说”的文件夹。剩下的实习期里，你的周末回来了。

career.en: Perfect Timing
career.zh: 来得真是时候

career.en: Days before your proposal, the company you interned at emails a full-time offer, with a deadline. Your slides are 60% done. The salary section is 100% done.
career.zh: 开题前几天，你实习过的公司发来全职 offer，还带着截止日期。你的 PPT 做了 60%，offer 的薪资部分你读了 3 遍。

career.en: Ask them to wait until after
career.zh: 请对方等你开完题

career.en: They give you a month. You go back to slide 23 calmer than you expected.
career.zh: 对方给了你一个月。你回到第 23 页，比预想的平静。

career.en: "We can do one week." Two big decisions now share the same week.
career.zh: “最多一周。”两件大事挤进了同一周。

career.en: Tell {advisor} about it
career.zh: 告诉 {advisor}

career.en: {advisor} says congratulations, then "slides first". You keep the offer and your focus.
career.zh: {advisor}先说了恭喜，然后说“先做 PPT”。offer 保住了，注意力也保住了。

career.en: {advisor} goes quiet, then asks how the slides are going. They seem a little worried.
career.zh: {advisor}沉默了一下，然后问你 PPT 做得怎么样了。看起来有点担心。

career.en: Decline: you're finishing the PhD
career.zh: 拒绝：先把博士读完

career.en: You say not yet. They say the door stays open, which might even be true. The slides get your full attention.
career.zh: 你说暂时不考虑。对方说大门永远敞开，这话说不定还是真的。你全心扑回了 PPT。

career.en: Two Things Due Friday
career.zh: 周五双 DDL

career.en: A university fellowship wants a two-page research statement by Friday. Friday is also the deadline for {project}. Both want your best writing, and you have enough for one.
career.zh: 一个校级奖学金要你周五前交两页研究陈述。周五也是 {project} 的截稿日。两边都要你最好的文笔，可你只够精力写好一份。

career.en: Statement first, paper second
career.zh: 先写陈述，再写论文

career.en: The statement is the clearest thing you've written all year. A month later you win the award, which is small but looks good on your CV.
career.zh: 这份陈述是你今年写得最清楚的东西。一个月后你拿到了这个奖，奖不大，但写在简历上很好看。

career.en: The statement is good and the paper is rushed. A month later, the fellowship sends a polite no.
career.zh: 陈述写得不错，论文却很仓促。一个月后，奖学金发来一封客气的拒信。

career.en: Paper first, statement overnight
career.zh: 先写论文，陈述熬夜写

career.en: The paper goes in strong. The statement, written at 3 am, says "robust" seven times and wins nothing.
career.zh: 论文交得很漂亮。凌晨 3 点写的陈述里出现了七次“鲁棒”，什么也没拿到。

career.en: Skip the fellowship this year
career.zh: 今年先不申奖学金

career.en: You have one deadline instead of two. There will be other fellowships.
career.zh: 两个截止变成了一个。奖学金年年有，不差这一回。

career.en: Perfect for Your Background
career.zh: 与你的背景完美契合

career.en: A recruiter writes: "Your background in transformers is a perfect fit!" The role maintains electrical transformers for a power company. The pay is honestly not bad.
career.zh: 一位猎头写道：“你的 Transformer 背景与我们非常匹配！”岗位是给电力公司维护变压器。说实话，工资还不错。

career.en: A recruiter says your NLP experience is perfect for their role. They mean Neuro-Linguistic Programming, as a life coach. There is a webinar.
career.zh: 一位猎头说你的 NLP 经历非常适合对方公司的岗位。人家说的是“神经语言程序学”，岗位是成功学讲师。还附赠一场线上公开课。

career.en: Take the call, just to see
career.zh: 接个电话，看看再说

career.en: After twenty minutes of friendly confusion, you both know a little about a whole other field.
career.zh: 二十分钟友好的鸡同鸭讲之后，你们俩都对另一个领域多了点了解。

career.en: Reply with a polite correction
career.zh: 礼貌地纠正一下

career.en: They thank you and pass your profile to a colleague who hires for actual machine learning roles.
career.zh: 对方道了谢，把你的资料转给了一位真招机器学习岗的同事。

career.en: They reply: "Even better! Are you free Tuesday?"
career.zh: 对方回复：“那更好了！周二有空吗？”

career.en: Forward it to the lab chat
career.zh: 转发到组群

career.en: The lab chat loses it. {labmate} makes it the channel topic for a month.
career.zh: 组群笑疯了。{labmate} 把它设成了群公告，挂了一个月。

career.en: The Pet Topic
career.zh: 教授的心头好

career.en: Your job talk lands. Then one professor asks how it connects to their favorite topic, and the next twenty minutes of Q&A are about that topic. Other hands slowly go down.
career.zh: 你的 job talk 很成功。然后一位教授问，这和自己最喜欢的课题有什么联系，接下来二十分钟的问答全围着那个课题转。其他举着的手慢慢放下了。

career.en: Engage with their topic seriously
career.zh: 认真回应这个话题

career.en: You find a real link. The professor beams, and you now have one very loud supporter in the hiring meeting.
career.zh: 你还真找到了两者的联系。那位教授笑开了花，招聘讨论会上你多了一个嗓门很大的支持者。

career.en: You improvise a connection. They correct it, for ten minutes, with diagrams.
career.zh: 你临场编了个关联。对方花了十分钟纠正你，还画了图。

career.en: "Great point, let's talk at dinner"
career.zh: “好问题，我们晚饭时聊”

career.en: Three more people get to ask questions. The search chair notices how you handled the room.
career.zh: 又有三个人得以提问。招聘委员会主席注意到了你控场的本事。

career.en: They follow up anyway. Two hands stay down for good.
career.zh: 对方还是追问不休。有两只手再也没举起来。

career.en: Promise to read their paper
career.zh: 答应读对方的论文

career.en: They email you the PDF before you leave the room. You read it at the hotel. At dinner, they ask what you thought.
career.zh: 你还没走出会议室，对方就把 PDF 发到了你邮箱。你在酒店读完了。晚饭时，对方问你读后感。

career.en: That's My Thesis
career.zh: 这不就是我的博士论文吗

career.en: An industry interviewer asks: "How would you evaluate our AI features with real users?" You have spent five years on exactly this question. You have four minutes.
career.zh: 一位业界面试官问：“你会怎么用真实用户评估我们的 AI 功能？”你在这个问题上花了整整五年。现在你有四分钟。

career.en: Give the four-minute version
career.zh: 讲四分钟精简版

career.en: You keep it clear and concrete and finish on time. The interviewer stops taking notes and starts nodding.
career.zh: 你讲得清楚具体，准时收尾。面试官不再记笔记，开始点头。

career.en: You reach minute four of a forty-minute answer. They thank you for the overview.
career.zh: 一个四十分钟的回答，你刚讲到第四分钟。对方感谢你做的“概述”。

career.en: Ask what their features do first
career.zh: 先问清楚功能是干什么的

career.en: The question turns into a design session. At the end they ask, half joking, "Can you start in June?"
career.zh: 问答变成了一场设计讨论。最后对方半开玩笑地问：“6 月能入职吗？”

career.en: Everything they could tell you is under NDA. You both stare at the question.
career.zh: 对方能说的全在保密协议里。你们俩对着这个问题大眼瞪小眼。

career.en: Pull up your thesis framework slide
career.zh: 调出博士论文框架图

career.en: Five years fit on one slide. They ask for a copy for their team, which is either flattering or worrying.
career.zh: 五年青春浓缩成了一页 PPT。对方要了一份拿回去给团队看，这到底是夸你还是该担心，不好说。

data.en: The 11 pm Shift
data.zh: 深夜专场

data.en: Your clinician annotators are careful, and only free after their shifts end around 11 pm. The questions start arriving at midnight.
data.zh: 你请的临床医生标注员都很细致，但要等晚上 11 点左右下班后才有空。问题从半夜开始源源不断地来。

data.en: Be online at 11 pm
data.zh: 晚上 11 点准时在线

data.en: You answer questions until 1 am, all week. Annotation finishes early, and so does your sleep.
data.zh: 整整一周，你每天回答问题到凌晨 1 点。标注提前完工，你的睡眠也提前收工。

data.en: This is your hour anyway
data.zh: 反正这是你的黄金时段

data.en: Night Owl
data.zh: 夜猫子

data.en: Midnight is your best hour. The annotators start calling you "the night desk".
data.zh: 午夜正是你状态最好的时候。标注员们开始叫你“夜间客服”。

data.en: Write a FAQ, answer mornings
data.zh: 写份 FAQ，早上统一回复

data.en: The FAQ covers most questions. The rest wait until morning, and so does the annotation.
data.zh: FAQ 解答了大部分问题。剩下的要等到早上，标注也跟着等。

data.en: Host a Saturday labeling brunch
data.zh: 周六组个标注早午餐局

data.en: Bagels work. Six annotators label 400 examples in four hours, and nobody is up past ten.
data.zh: 贝果攻势奏效。六位标注员四小时标了 400 条，没有一个人熬过十点。

data.en: Only two annotators show up, so you get excellent bagels and very few labels.
data.zh: 只来了两位标注员。贝果很香，标注很少。

data.en: 500 Examples
data.zh: 500 条样本

data.en: It's Friday evening. The annotators start Monday, and you need 500 gold-standard examples to check them against.
data.zh: 周五晚上。标注员周一开工，你得先准备 500 条金标准样本来检验他们。

data.en: Annotate all 500 this weekend
data.zh: 这个周末标完 500 条

data.en: By Sunday night you know this data better than anyone alive. Your eyes would like a word.
data.zh: 到周日晚上，你比世上任何人都了解这份数据。你的眼睛在申请带薪休假。

data.en: Split them with {labmate}
data.zh: 和 {labmate} 平分

data.en: They label 250 and find two holes in your guidelines. You buy lunch, and would happily buy ten.
data.zh: 对方标了 250 条，还发现了你标注指南里的两个漏洞。你请了顿午饭，心想请十顿也心甘情愿。

data.en: "I have a deadline too." You do 400 of them alone, more slowly than you'd like.
data.zh: “抱歉，我也有截稿。”你一个人标了 400 条，比预想的慢。

data.en: Do 100, call it a pilot
data.zh: 标 100 条，就当预实验

data.en: You label 100 careful examples and call it a pilot. Nobody needs to know it was meant to be 500.
data.zh: 你仔细标了 100 条，对外统一口径：这是预实验。没人需要知道原计划是 500 条。

data.en: Guidelines v15
data.zh: 指南 v15

data.en: You open annotation_guidelines_v15.docx. Version 14 fixed one ambiguity and created two new ones. Agreement went from 0.41 to 0.44.
data.zh: 你打开了标注指南_最终版_v15.docx。第 14 版消除了一处歧义，又制造了两处新的。一致性从 0.41 涨到了 0.44。

data.en: Write version 16, properly
data.zh: 认真写个第 16 版

data.en: Version 16 has a decision tree and twelve worked examples. Agreement jumps to 0.71.
data.zh: 第 16 版有一棵决策树和十二个完整示例。一致性跃升到 0.71。

data.en: Run a calibration session
data.zh: 开一次校准会

data.en: An hour on ten hard cases gets everyone on the same page. The guidelines barely change, and agreement still climbs.
data.zh: 花一小时过了十个疑难样本，大家终于达成了共识。指南几乎没改，一致性照样上涨。

data.en: The session turns into a debate about a single example. As far as you know, it's still going.
data.zh: 校准会变成了围绕一条样本的辩论。据你所知，现在还没吵完。

data.en: Freeze v15 and annotate
data.zh: 定稿 v15，开始标注

data.en: The annotators cheer. The agreement score does not.
data.zh: 标注员们欢呼起来。一致性分数没有。

data.en: Seen It Before
data.zh: 似曾相识
